title: fix(core): reject comma from AxiosHeaders valid header name pattern
description: :surfer: ## Summary `isValidHeaderName` in `lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js` incorrectly accepts a comma (`,`) as part of a valid header name. Per [RFC 7230 §3.2.6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7230#section-3.2.6), a header field-name is a `token` made only of `tchar` characters, and a comma is explicitly listed as a `delimiter`, not a `tchar`. Because `AxiosHeaders#set(header, ...)` uses `isValidHeaderName` to decide whether a string argument is a single header *name* (vs. a raw multi-header text blob to hand to `parseHeaders`), a comma-containing string is wrongly treated as one literal header name instead of being rejected or parsed as raw header text. The invalid name then survives untouched through `AxiosHeaders` and only fails later, as a confusing low-level error thrown by Node's `http` module (`ERR_INVALID_HTTP_TOKEN`) or the browser's `XHR`/`fetch` header APIs (`SyntaxError`), instead of being caught consistently at the axios layer. ### Repro (before fix) ```js import AxiosHeaders from './lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js'; const headers = new AxiosHeaders(); headers.set('X-Foo,Bar', 'value'); console.log(headers.has('X-Foo,Bar')); // true (should be false / rejected) ``` ## Linked issue N/A — one-character regex fix with a clear RFC citation and reproduction included above; no separate issue filed. ## Changes - `lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js`: removed `,` from the `isValidHeaderName` character class. - `tests/unit/axiosHeaders.test.js`: added a regression test asserting a comma-containing string is not treated as a valid header name. - `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`: added a Bug Fixes entry. #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) — N/A, `isValidHeaderName` is an internal helper, not public API - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) --- ## Summary by cubic Reject commas in header names in AxiosHeaders per RFC 7230, and validate names when storing headers so all input paths are covered. This prevents invalid names like "X-Foo,Bar" from being accepted and failing later in Node/browser APIs. **Description** - Summary of changes: removed comma from `isValidHeaderName` pattern; validate header name at storage time in `AxiosHeaders#set` for strings, objects, maps/iterables, and raw header lines; updated changelog with PR reference. - Reasoning: comma is a delimiter, not a token; reject early to align with RFC 7230 and surface clear errors. - Additional context: invalid names are now ignored on set rather than slipping through to transport layers. **Docs** - Add a short note in `/docs/` headers section that header names must be RFC 7230 tokens (no commas). **Testing** - Added a regression test that verifies comma-containing names are rejected across all input paths; no further tests needed. **Semantic version impact** - Patch: behavior correction only; no public API changes. Written for commit 6d8ea08eeeac49af65471e2558713bac52d9bf45. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(utils): serialize Map values in toJSONObject
description: :surfer: ## Summary `#11044` recently fixed `utils.toJSONObject` to serialize `Set` values as arrays instead of empty objects, but left `Map` with the same gap: a `Map` has no own enumerable string keys, so `forEach`'s `Object.keys(map)` returns `[]` and the map silently becomes `{}`. `AxiosError#toJSON()` uses `toJSONObject` to serialize `config`, so any `Map` reachable from an axios request config currently vanishes from the serialized error instead of surfacing its contents. ### Repro (before fix) ```js import utils from './lib/utils.js'; console.log(utils.toJSONObject(new Map([['a', 1], ['b', 2]]))); // {} console.log(JSON.stringify(utils.toJSONObject({ data: new Map([['x', 1]]) }))); // {"data":{}} ``` ### After fix ```js console.log(utils.toJSONObject(new Map([['a', 1], ['b', 2]]))); // [['a',1],['b',2]] ``` A `Map` is serialized as an array of `[key, value]` pairs (mirroring `Array.from(map.entries())`), since — unlike `Set` — both the key and the value need to be preserved and a `Map` key is not restricted to strings. ## Linked issue N/A — direct follow-up to the `Set` fix in #11044, same root cause and same fix pattern, with a reproduction included above. ## Changes - `lib/utils.js`: added `isMap`, and a `Map` branch in `toJSONObject` that serializes entries as `[key, value]` pairs (mirrors the existing `Set` branch). - `tests/unit/utils.test.js`: added a `Map handling` test suite mirroring the existing `Set handling` suite (flat, nested-in-object, cross-realm, recursive, undefined-value skipping, shared-reference DAG, self-cycle). - `tests/unit/core/AxiosError.test.js`: added a test asserting `AxiosError#toJSON()` serializes `Map` values in the config snapshot. - `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`: added a Bug Fixes entry. #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) — N/A, `toJSONObject`/`isMap` are internal helpers, not public API - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) --- ## Summary by cubic Serialize `Map` values in `utils.toJSONObject` as arrays of `[key, value]`, and emit `"[WeakMap]"`/`"[WeakSet]"` placeholders so `AxiosError#toJSON()` preserves Map data and the presence of Weak collections in config snapshots. Also drop entries whose key or value resolves to a cycle or `undefined`. ## Description - Summary of changes - Added `isMap`, `isWeakSet`, and `isWeakMap` checks; added branches in `toJSONObject`. - `Map` serializes to `[key, value]` pairs; skips entries with `undefined` keys/values (including cyclic keys/values); supports nested and cross-realm maps. - `WeakMap`/`WeakSet` serialize as `"[WeakMap]"`/`"[WeakSet]"` placeholders. - Updated changelog entry. - Reasoning - `Map` previously serialized to `{}` and lost data; `WeakMap`/`WeakSet` also collapsed to `{}` and hid their presence. - Additional context - Follow-up to the recent `Set` serialization fix for consistent error output. ## Docs Add notes in `/docs/`: - `AxiosError#toJSON()` now serializes `Map` values as `[key, value]` arrays. - `WeakMap`/`WeakSet` appear as placeholder strings. - Entries with cyclic or `undefined` keys/values are skipped. ## Testing - Added unit tests in `tests/unit/utils.test.js` for `Map` (flat, nested, cross-realm, nested maps, `undefined` skipping, DAGs, self-cycles, cyclic key drop). - Added tests for `WeakSet`/`WeakMap` placeholders (top-level and nested). - Added `tests/unit/core/AxiosError.test.js` to assert `AxiosError#toJSON()` includes `Map` values in the config snapshot. - No further tests needed. ## Semantic version impact - Patch: bug fix with no breaking API changes. Written for commit 9e37958a48ff5903f9e5d1ede93be50620d2ac6b. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix: strip DQUOTE delimiters in parseTokens per RFC 9110
description: When a parameter value is quoted with DQUOTE characters (e.g. oundary=----boundary123), parseTokens returned the quotes as part of the value. This fix strips leading and trailing DQUOTE characters from parameter values per RFC 9110. --- ## Summary by cubic Fix token parameter parsing to strip surrounding DQUOTE characters per RFC 9110, so values like boundary="----boundary123" are returned without quotes. Also refreshes CI, docs, and repo configs to harden security and improve maintenance. **Description** - Summary of changes - Strip leading/trailing DQUOTE from parameter values in `parseTokens`. - Add `CODEOWNERS`, Prettier, devcontainer; pin and harden GitHub Actions; add lockfile-lint, bundle-size, reproducible-build, and security scans. - Migrate/expand docs to VitePress under `/docs/`, add a threat model, and remove legacy scripts and bower. - Reasoning - Aligns with RFC 9110: quoted-string delimiters must not be included in the parsed value. - Prevents incorrect header parameter values (e.g., `Content-Type` boundaries, `Content-Disposition` filenames). - Additional context - Only strips a single pair of wrapping quotes; interior content is unchanged. - Low risk: some callers may have relied on quotes being present. **Docs** - Add a note to `docs/*/pages/advanced/headers.md` explaining that quoted parameter values are unquoted during parsing (example: `boundary="foo"` → `boundary=foo`). Mirror the note in README and the changelog in `/docs/`. **Testing** - Add/ensure unit tests for `parseTokens` covering DQUOTE-wrapped values, empty values, and common headers like `Content-Type` with `boundary`. - CI updates: vitest runs in `run-ci.yml`; lockfile lint, bundle-size, reproducible build, and workflow security scans are enabled. **Semantic version impact** - Patch: spec-compliant bug fix with no API changes. Potential minor behavior change if consumers expected quotes to be retained. Written for commit 621aa73557fb6c182e1889e0663d26eda9fb3dbd. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(core): synchronous interceptors swallow errors and proceed with request
description: Palade identified a critical logic defect in Axios's synchronous request interceptor path: when an `onFulfilled` handler throws, Axios calls that interceptor's paired `onRejected` handler but previously ignored the handler's result and could still dispatch the request. This could bypass validation or security checks when the rejection handler signaled failure by returning a rejected Promise. This PR preserves Axios's existing paired-handler behavior while making terminal failures stop request dispatch: 1. Run each synchronous request interceptor's `onFulfilled` handler with the last valid config. 2. If it throws and has no paired `onRejected`, reject with the original error and do not dispatch. 3. If the paired `onRejected` throws or returns a rejected Promise, reject with that failure and do not dispatch. 4. If the paired `onRejected` returns normally or returns a fulfilled Promise, treat the error as handled and dispatch with the last valid config; the handler's return value does not replace the config. 5. Stop running subsequent request interceptors after the thrown error, and pass terminal failures through response rejection interceptors. :surfer: --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes sync request interceptor error handling in `axios`. Thrown errors no longer send a request unless the paired `onRejected` resolves; we keep the last valid config and route terminal errors to response rejection interceptors. ## Description - Summary of changes - Do not dispatch when a sync request interceptor throws with no `onRejected`. - Do not dispatch when its `onRejected` throws or returns a rejected Promise. - If `onRejected` resolves (including `undefined` or a fulfilled Promise), dispatch with the last valid config; ignore its return value. - Stop running remaining request interceptors after the thrown error. - Terminal errors flow to response rejection interceptors. - Reasoning - Prevents accidental dispatch after validation failures. - Preserves existing paired-handler behavior. - Additional context - Pre-release changelog and docs notes updated; synced with `v1.x`. ## Docs Update `/docs/` Interceptors to explain sync error flow and examples: - Throw in `onFulfilled` calls the paired `onRejected` and stops other request interceptors. - If `onRejected` resolves, continue with the last valid config; if it throws or rejects, do not dispatch. - Add examples for blocking (reject) vs logging (resolve). ## Testing Browser tests added: - No `onRejected` -> reject with original error; no request sent. - `onRejected` rejects -> no request sent. - `onRejected` resolves -> request sent with last valid config; return value ignored. - `onRejected` throws -> reject with that error; no request sent. - Terminal sync errors reach response `onRejected`. ## Semantic version impact Patch: fixes incorrect error handling without changing the public API. Written for commit 6a8d43156d7ae3957feee0e643e657702b46e9af. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(interceptors): replace handlers array with Map to prevent memory leak
description: ## Summary Resolves a memory leak in `InterceptorManager` caused by the unbounded growth of the `handlers` array. Currently, calling `.eject(id)` sets the index to `null` instead of removing the element, leaving behind tombstone slots that accumulate over the life of the instance. Replacing the array with a `Map` allows ejected interceptors to be completely removed from memory. ## Linked issue Closes #11070 ## Changes - Migrated `this.handlers` to a `Map` structure and used an incrementing `_idCounter` for unique IDs in `InterceptorManager`. - Updated TypeScript declaration files (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) to reflect `handlers` as a `Map`. - Updated browser tests to reset `handlers` to a `Map` instead of `[]` in `afterEach` and to assert using `.size` instead of `.length`. #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes a memory leak in `InterceptorManager` by replacing the internal handlers array with a `Map` so ejected interceptors are fully removed. Also stabilizes iteration to avoid visiting handlers added or removed during a run. **Description** - Summary of changes - Switched `handlers` to `Map` with a Symbol-keyed incrementing ID; `use()` returns the ID. - `eject(id)` deletes the entry; `clear()` calls `handlers.clear()`. - `forEach` snapshots `Map` keys and looks up each key to skip ejected handlers and ignore newly added ones. - Updated types in `index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts` to `Map`. - Reasoning - The array left null “tombstones” after `eject`, causing unbounded growth. - Additional context - Browser tests now initialize with `new Map()` and assert using `.size`. **Docs** - Update `/docs/` to note the internal switch to a `Map` for interceptors; public API is unchanged. **Testing** - Adjusted existing browser tests to use `Map` and `.size`. No new tests needed; `eject()` and `clear()` behavior is covered. **Semantic version impact** - Patch. Public API remains the same; only internal storage changed. Written for commit e00929bd4c99b4025a8b1f3d426de6eef9c10d56. Summary will update on new commits.

title: docs: scope the provenance claim in SECURITY.md to attested versions
description: While reading SECURITY.md I tried the release-verification steps it describes, and I think the current wording promises slightly more than the registry shows. Sharing what I found in case it's useful. The section says every axios tarball on npm carries a provenance attestation, and asks readers to treat a missing one as a potential supply-chain incident. Checking npm's attestation endpoint for each of the 142 published versions, 89 have no attestation: everything up to 1.6.0, versions 0.29.0–0.30.3, and 1.13.3 (its neighbors 1.13.2 and 1.13.4 do have them). For example: ``` curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/attestations/axios@0.30.3 # 404 curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/attestations/axios@1.18.1 # 200 ``` Since 0.x is a supported line (and 0.30.0 is what the `old-version` dist-tag points to), someone following the verification instructions on those releases could raise a false alarm — or, worse, get used to shrugging off missing attestations, which would blunt a genuinely useful check. This PR only narrows the wording to the versions where the guarantee holds. I may well be missing context — if the gaps at 1.13.3 and 0.29.0–0.30.3 are known and documented somewhere I didn't find, happy to adjust the numbers or close this. :surfer: *Prepared with AI assistance, reviewed and submitted by me.* --- ## Summary by cubic Scopes the provenance attestation claim in SECURITY.md to only the `axios` versions that are actually attested, and lists explicit exceptions to prevent false alarms. Aligns release verification guidance with npm’s per‑version attestations. ## Description - Summary of changes - Set attestation defaults at v1.6.1 (1.x) and v0.31.0 (0.x). - Noted exceptions: v0.28.0–v0.28.1 are attested; v1.13.3 and v0.29.0–v0.30.3 are not. - Clarified that incident reporting applies only to versions listed as attested. - Reasoning - Previous wording implied all releases were attested and could trigger false positives. - Additional context - Version statuses verified against npm’s per‑version dist.attestations. - Merged latest `v1.x` into this branch; no content changes. ## Docs - Mirror the updated provenance wording in `/docs/` anywhere release verification is described. ## Testing - No code changes; no tests needed. - Optional: run `npm audit signatures` on `axios@1.18.x` (attested) and `axios@0.30.3` (not) to validate examples. ## Semantic version impact - None. Documentation-only change. Written for commit 34b85b81ad326e6fb4c93682982285ba199dec67. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(interceptors): remove ejected handlers
description: :surfer: ## Summary - remove ejected interceptor records instead of leaving null slots behind - keep stable interceptor ids so stale ids cannot remove later handlers after compaction - add focused InterceptorManager regression tests for compaction, stale ids, and order preservation ## Verification - npm run test:vitest:unit -- tests/unit/core/InterceptorManager.test.js - npx eslint lib/core/InterceptorManager.js tests/unit/core/InterceptorManager.test.js --- ## Summary by cubic Removes ejected interceptors instead of leaving null slots and introduces stable numeric IDs to prevent stale removals. Adds focused tests to verify compaction, order, and stale ID safety. **Description** - Summary of changes - Remove ejected handlers with splice; no more null slots. - Add stable numeric IDs via a private symbol and `nextId`. - Keep `forEach` simple since there are no nulls to skip. - Reasoning - Avoid sparse arrays and reduce memory growth. - Prevent stale IDs from removing later handlers. - Preserve insertion order after ejections. - Additional context - Public API is unchanged: `use` returns a number; `eject(id)` still works. - Behavior is backward compatible and internal-only. **Docs** - Update `/docs/` interceptor docs to clarify: - IDs are stable and not tied to array indices. - Ejected handlers are removed, not set to null. - `forEach` no longer needs to account for null entries. **Testing** - Added unit tests in `tests/unit/core/InterceptorManager.test.js`: - Ensures no null slots remain after many add/eject cycles. - Verifies stale IDs cannot remove newer handlers. - Confirms insertion order is preserved after middle ejections. **Semantic version impact** - Patch: internal behavior change with no public API breakage. Written for commit 15424b918204778bbe74017348d32070fabaa48b. Summary will update on new commits.

title: feat(types): Allow the Params property to be typed, instead of `any`
description:
> [!NOTE] > If you, due to time constraints or otherwise, won't be able to review this PR within the next year, please just say so right away and save us all time and nerves. Thanks in advance. Similar to/Follow-up to #1061 Resubmission of #6807 ## Summary Currently, it is not possible to have `AxiosRequestConfig.params` correctly typed—it will always be `any`. This PR changes that. ## Linked issue Closes #4954 ## Changes * Makes `AxiosRequestConfig.params` generic, so it can be typed/the type be inferred #### Checklist - [ ] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) - [ ] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) - [x] The changes are not stale - [x] The PR has a reviewer - [x] The PR has no unaddressed feedback --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a `params` generic to `axios` request configs and propagates it across the public types for stronger typing and inference, with no runtime changes. Default request methods and `AxiosPromise` now preserve the request data and params types on `response.config`. ## Description - Summary of changes - Added `P` to `AxiosRequestConfig` and propagated to `RawAxiosRequestConfig`, `InternalAxiosRequestConfig`, `AxiosDefaults`, `CreateAxiosDefaults`, `AxiosResponse`, `AxiosError`, `CanceledError`, `isCancel()`, `isAxiosError()`, all request aliases and callable `AxiosInstance`, adapters, `AxiosPromise`, and `mergeConfig()` in both ESM (`index.d.ts`) and CJS (`index.d.cts`). - Introduced an internal `AxiosResponseDefault` to keep existing generic positions; defaulted request aliases now return `AxiosResponse` so `response.config.data` and `response.config.params` mirror the request types. - Made `CustomParamsSerializer

title: feat(xhr): read XSRF cookie via async Cookie Store API when available
description: ## Summary Closes #10826 Implements the maintainer-specified change from #10826: the XHR adapter now reads the XSRF cookie through the asynchronous Cookie Store API (`window.cookieStore`) when the browser provides it, avoiding synchronous, main-thread-blocking `document.cookie` access (whatwg/html#11658). Browsers without `cookieStore` (notably Safari) use the existing `document.cookie` path, unchanged. This supersedes the approach in #7040 and addresses each blocker from its close comment (see checklist below). ## What changed | File | Change | |------|--------| | `lib/helpers/cookies.js` | Adds an async cookieStore read path alongside the existing document.cookie implementation; non-standard-env no-op shim retained for both | | `lib/helpers/resolveConfig.js` | XSRF read may now resolve asynchronously; `own(key)` guard, `withXSRFToken` gating, and `encodeUTF8` untouched | | `lib/adapters/xhr.js` | Minimal change to consume the (possibly async) resolved config — no re-indent of `dispatchXhrRequest` | | `test/...` | New tests mocking `window.cookieStore` explicitly (async branch verified to execute), fallback path, raw-value round-trip, and security-guard regression tests | ## Spec compliance (from #10826) - [x] **XHR-only** — fetch adapter untouched - [x] **Automatic, not opt-in** — runtime `window.cookieStore` detection; no new public config - [x] **Raw value round-trip** — no `decodeURIComponent`/`encodeURIComponent` on the cookieStore path; encoding remains only on the `document.cookie` path - [x] **Security hardening preserved** — `own(key)` guard (GHSA-q8qp-cvcw-x6jj), strict `withXSRFToken` check (GHSA-xx6v-rp6x-q39c), `encodeUTF8` all intact and covered by tests - [x] **Non-standard-env no-op preserved** — Web Worker / React Native shim retained for the new export - [x] **resolveConfig callers audited** — [list each caller checked and outcome] - [x] **No behaviour change without cookieStore** — fallback path identical; verified by tests ## Avoiding the #7040 blockers - Based on current `v1.x` head — no regression of prior CVE fixes - No double encoding — cookieStore values passed raw in both directions - Non-standard-env fallback retained - No broad re-indent of the XHR adapter; diff is confined to the XSRF read path - Auto-detection rather than an opt-in flag ## Test plan - `npm test` — full suite green, new tests visibly executed (output attached) - New tests differentiate the cookieStore branch from the document.cookie branch by mocking `window.cookieStore` directly, rather than asserting via `document.cookie` (which co-stores and cannot distinguish the two) - Build (`npm run build`) verified ## Out of scope (per #10826) No general async-resolution work beyond the XSRF read, no fetch adapter changes, no new public config options. --- ## Summary by cubic Reads the XSRF cookie via the async `window.cookieStore` API in the XHR adapter when available, falling back to `document.cookie`. This avoids blocking the main thread without changing behavior on unsupported browsers. **Description** - Added `readAsync`/`writeAsync`/`removeAsync` to `lib/helpers/cookies.js` using `window.cookieStore` with a no-op shim for non-standard envs. - Updated `resolveConfig()` to optionally return a Promise when `cookieStore` is present (sync path unchanged otherwise). - Updated `lib/adapters/xhr.js` to handle sync/async config resolution and to respect cancellation/abort during resolve before dispatch. - Preserved XSRF gating, `own(key)` checks, `encodeUTF8`, and raw cookie values on the `cookieStore` path. - No changes to the fetch adapter or non-standard environments. **Docs, Testing, and Semantic version impact** - Docs: Update `/docs/` to note XHR uses `window.cookieStore` when available, falling back to `document.cookie`. Touch cookies/XSRF docs for `withXSRFToken`, `xsrfCookieName`, and `xsrfHeaderName`. No new config. - Testing: Added browser tests for async `cookieStore` reads, fallback path, raw-value round-trip, and gating. Test setup disables global `cookieStore` by default and mocks it per test. No further tests needed. - Semantic version impact: Minor (feature behind capability detection; no breaking changes). Written for commit b4cbf713e3dce7d186e99e514e3606259d31e561. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(interceptors): trim trailing ejected handlers
description: ## Summary Fixes unbounded sparse-array growth in `InterceptorManager` caused by ejected interceptors leaving trailing `null` tombstones. The implementation preserves the existing `handlers` array and public types. Trailing tombstones are removed after ejection, with compaction deferred during iteration so newly registered interceptors are not accidentally included in the current interceptor chain. ## Linked issue Closes #11070 ## Changes - Trim trailing `null` handlers after interceptor ejection. - Defer compaction while `forEach()` is iterating to preserve existing snapshot behavior. - Keep `handlers` as an array and leave ESM/CommonJS declarations unchanged. - Add focused tests covering repeated registration/ejection, interior tombstones, mutation during iteration, and `clear()` behavior. - Add the fix to `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`. ## Testing Ran suit locally #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (N/A — public API and types are unchanged) - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) --- ## Summary by cubic Prevents `InterceptorManager` handler array growth by trimming trailing ejected handlers and using monotonic, non-reused IDs. Also clears stale handler entries when the handlers array is replaced or reset in place; iteration behavior and public types stay the same, and compaction runs after iteration. ## Description - Trim trailing `null` entries after `eject()`; keep interior tombstones. - Use monotonic IDs from `use()`; ignore stale IDs after `clear()`, in-place reset, or array replacement. - Clear stale ID-to-handler entries when `handlers` is replaced or emptied in place; resync on `clear()`. - Defer trimming during `forEach()`; compact once iteration ends. - Preserve `handlers` as an array and keep ESM/CJS types unchanged. - Closes #11070. ## Docs - Update `/docs/` (interceptors): - Trailing tombstones are trimmed after ejection. - IDs from `use()` are monotonic and are not reused; stale IDs are ignored after `clear()`, in-place reset, or array replacement. - Iteration visits only handlers present when it starts. - Recommend `.clear()` over replacing the array or changing its length. ## Testing - Added `tests/unit/core/InterceptorManager.test.js`: - No growth under repeated register/eject cycles. - No ID reuse; stale IDs are ignored after `clear()`/replacement/in-place reset. - Deferred compaction during iteration; compaction after. - ID invalidation when `handlers` is replaced; `clear()` during iteration; in-place resets do not leak entries. - Updated browser tests to call `axios.interceptors.request.clear()` and `.response.clear()`. ## Semantic version impact Patch: bug fix with backward-compatible behavior. Written for commit a4cc01856d6ad2bfc8b8a6a1576134230d97e70d. Summary will update on new commits.

v1.18.1 — June 21, 2026

This release focuses on Node HTTP adapter fixes, safer AxiosError serialisation, runtime/type correctness fixes, documentation updates, and dependency maintenance.

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • AxiosError Serialisation: Made AxiosError#cause non-enumerable to prevent circular JSON serialisation failures when errors include nested causes. (#10913)
  • Node HTTP Adapter: Guarded socket.setKeepAlive for proxy agent streams, accepted path-only URLs when socketPath is configured, deferred environment proxy handling to Node, and explicitly passed maxBodyLength through to follow-redirects. (#10917, #10930, #10942, #10993)
  • Runtime and Type Correctness: Fixed several runtime crashes, type definition mismatches, and incorrect error handling paths. (#10959, #11021)
  • AxiosURLSearchParams: Switched the encoder callback to an arrow function so encoder.call(this) receives the AxiosURLSearchParams instance correctly. (#11019)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Documentation: Documented sensitive headers and status transition behaviour, prepared cleaned-up docs, added Deno install instructions, and clarified that request data is request-specific (#11007, #11010, #11023, #11025)

  • Dependencies: Bumped vite, rollup, form-data, js-yaml, and multer across the root project, docs, smoke tests, and module test workspaces. (#11011, #11012, #11013, #11014, #11015, #11016, #11017, #11026)

Full Changelog

v1.18.0 — June 13, 2026

This release hardens redirect and URL handling, improves the validateStatus configuration semantics, and includes updates to documentation, dependencies, and release metadata.

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Redirect Header Safety: Added Node HTTP adapter support for stripping caller-specified sensitive headers on cross-origin redirects, helping prevent custom auth headers such as API keys from leaking to another origin. (#10892)

  • URL And Request Hardening: Rejects malformed http: and https: URLs that omit // with ERR_INVALID_URL, while tightening prototype-pollution-safe config reads, stream size limits, FormData depth handling, data URL sizing, and local NO_PROXY matching. (#11000)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Status Validation: Added transitional.validateStatusUndefinedResolves so applications can opt in to treating validateStatus: undefined like the option was omitted, while validateStatus: null remains the explicit way to accept every status. (#10899)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

title: fix(xhr): reject navigation-canceled requests as ECONNABORTED
description: ## Summary Firefox 152 stopped firing `error` and `abort` for XHRs canceled by a document navigation, emitting only `readystatechange` and `loadend` ([bugzilla 1505389](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1505389), and Mozilla upstreamed a conformance test for it in [wpt#59603](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/59603)). Since `onerror`/`onabort` are what reject and null the request handle, and that null is the only thing making `onloadend` bail, `onloadend` became the only handler that runs. `settle()` then resolved the canceled request through its `!response.status` branch, so callers received a successful response carrying `status: 0` and an empty body. This rejects that case in the XHR adapter instead, with `ECONNABORTED` / `Request aborted`. That is the same error Firefox 151 produced for the identical cancellation, so an application sees no change in outcome across the Firefox update. Mozilla confirmed the old behavior on the bug ("only the onabort callback is called instead of onerror") and the patch that changed it is titled "Fires readystatechange and loadend intead of abort". `lib/core/settle.js` is deliberately untouched, because it is shared with the fetch adapter where an opaque `no-cors` response legitimately carries status 0. **Patch-level behavior change, not a breaking API change.** Browser requests whose response reaches `loadend` with status 0 previously resolved with an empty body and now reject with `ECONNABORTED` / `Request aborted`. Two consequences worth stating explicitly: - Reads over `file:`, which some environments report as status 0 on success, still resolve. The exemption looks at the scheme of the request URL, at the scheme of the page origin for relative URLs (which inherit it), and at `responseURL` where implemented. - The rejection is not suppressed by `validateStatus`. It never consulted it for status 0 anyway, since `!response.status` short-circuits ahead of it, and `onerror`/`onabort` reject unconditionally for the same reason: there is no response to validate. This is XHR-only. The fetch and Node HTTP adapters do not have the equivalent failure mode, and are unchanged. ## Linked issue Closes #11093 ## Changes - `lib/adapters/xhr.js`: reject with `ECONNABORTED` when `onloadend` is reached with status 0, excluding `file:` reads. - `tests/browser/requests.browser.test.js`: a rejection test for the non-`file:` case, and a resolve test for a relative `file:` read, placed next to the existing file-protocol test. - `tests/unit/adapters/xhr.test.js`: unit tests that drive the real adapter in Node with stubbed globals, covering the relative `file:` read without `responseURL` raised in review, plus reject and resolve controls for the other exemption sources. - `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`: entry under Bug Fixes. #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) - N/A, no public API change. The existing `ECONNABORTED` description ("timed out ... or aborted by the browser or its plugin") already covers this case. - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) ## Validation Run against this branch, on top of `v1.x` at 5097193 (1.19.0): ``` npm run lint exit 0 npm run build exit 0 npm run test:vitest:browser:headless 591 passed (chromium, firefox, webkit) ``` `npm run test:vitest:unit` has 2 failures in `tests/unit/adapters/fetch.test.js`, both of which reproduce identically on a pristine checkout of `v1.x`, so they are unrelated to this change. Each new assertion was mutation-tested: removing the guard fails the rejection tests, and dropping any of the three `file:` exemption sources fails a corresponding test. Note that Playwright's bundled Firefox is 151, which predates the behavior being fixed, so the regression cannot be reproduced through the browser runner. The tests use the existing `MockXMLHttpRequest`, whose `finish()` already fires only `onloadend`, which is exactly the Firefox 152 shape. The browser harness also cannot serve a page over `file:`, so the page-origin exemption is covered by the unit tests instead, which stub the globals before importing axios so the real adapter runs with a `file:` origin. :surfer: Investigated and written with AI assistance, reviewed before opening. --- ## Summary by cubic Reject navigation-canceled XHRs with status 0 as `ECONNABORTED` to prevent empty successes on Firefox 152+. Successful `file:` reads still resolve, including relative paths inferred from the page’s `file:` origin or via `responseURL`. - **Description** - XHR adapter now rejects on `loadend` with status 0 unless it’s a `file:` read (checks normalized request URL, page origin for relative URLs, and `responseURL`). - Added `normalizeURLForProtocolCheck` to match WHATWG URL preprocessing; used by XHR protocol checks and imported by `buildFullPath`. - Leaves `lib/core/settle.js` unchanged to avoid impacting fetch’s opaque `no-cors` responses. - Rejection occurs before `validateStatus`, since no response was received. - **Testing and Impact** - Browser tests: reject non-`file:` status 0; resolve absolute/relative `file:` reads, including via `responseURL`. - Unit tests: cover page-origin inference, URL normalization (leading spaces/C0 controls), and that `validateStatus` is not called. - Docs: update `/docs/` browser/XHR section to note status 0 on `loadend` rejects as `ECONNABORTED`, except successful `file:` reads; clarify `validateStatus` is not applied without a response. - Semantic version: Patch (XHR-only bug fix; Node and fetch adapters unchanged). Written for commit 27b9d9761cba6fe477dfa6104527523ba2450ad4. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix: core methodList, HTTP adapter errors, and add tests
description:
This recreates #11048 after the original fork branch was accidentally deleted.

## Problem

Axios supports per-method header defaults for `OPTIONS`, `PURGE`, `LINK`, `UNLINK`, and `QUERY`, but request header flattening removed only a subset of method buckets. Configuring the omitted buckets could therefore serialize structural objects as literal headers such as `options: [object Object]` or leak one method's defaults into another request.

The Node HTTP adapter also raised raw `TypeError` instances for invalid custom DNS lookup results and invalid or unsupported `httpVersion` values instead of the documented `AxiosError` shape.

## Changes

- Add a frozen `lib/core/methodList.js` containing every method represented by the runtime types and header defaults.
- Use the shared list to initialize defaults and remove all structural method buckets during request preparation.
- Reject invalid lookup addresses and `httpVersion` values with `AxiosError.ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE`.
- Route lookup validation failures through normal request error handling so the final error retains the correct per-request config without breaking cached HTTP/2 lookup identity.
- Replace the stale `timeoutMessage` merge-map key with `timeoutErrorMessage`. Supported string values already followed equivalent generic fallback behavior; this cleanup makes the intended merge strategy explicit.
- Record the user-visible fixes in `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`.

## Tests

- Dispatch every supported method through a custom adapter and verify that only its matching defaults apply and no method bucket becomes an outgoing header.
- Cover invalid lookup addresses, nonnumeric `httpVersion`, and unsupported numeric versions, including error code and config diagnostics.
- Preserve cached custom-DNS and HTTP/2 session-reuse coverage after rebasing onto current `v1.x`.

Local validation:

- `npm run test:vitest:unit -- tests/unit/axios.test.js tests/unit/adapters/http.test.js` — 250 passed.
- `npm run test:vitest:unit -- tests/unit/core/mergeConfig.test.js` — 62 passed.
- Focused ESLint passed for all changed source files.

:surfer: AI-assisted maintainer updates were applied after review.

title: fix(core): prevent sparse array growth in InterceptorManager (#11070)
description:
## Summary

This PR addresses issue #11070 where \InterceptorManager\ accumulated \
ull\ tombstones inside a sparse array upon calling \eject(id)\. In long-running applications or services that frequently add and eject interceptors (such as per-request authorization interceptors or retry mechanisms), \	his.handlers\ array grew indefinitely, leading to memory leaks and performance degradation on \ orEach\ iterations.

## Linked issue

Closes #11070

## Changes

- Refactored \InterceptorManager\ storage from a sparse array to a \Map()\ with incrementing integer IDs.
- Calling \eject(id)\ now removes the entry via \	his.handlers.delete(id)\, ensuring memory is freed and Map size shrinks back to 0.
- Added a non-enumerable getter for \.length\ on \	his.handlers\ Map for 100% backward compatibility with external code inspecting \handlers.length\.
- Updated TypeScript definitions in \index.d.ts\ and \index.d.cts\.
- Added unit tests in \	ests/unit/core/InterceptorManager.test.js\ including a 10,000-cycle stress test verifying zero sparse memory growth.

#### Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason)
- [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (\index.d.ts\ and \index.d.cts\)
- [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above)

title: fix(core): tolerate non-string stack when decorating request errors
description: Fixes #11108 The stack-decoration block in `Axios.prototype.request`'s catch handler guards `dummy.stack` only for truthiness. When the global `Error.prepareStackTrace` is overridden to return a non-string (a common instrumentation pattern — APM agents and `callsites`-style libraries return raw CallSite data), `dummy.stack` is truthy but not a string, `.indexOf('\n')` throws, and **the original request error is replaced by an unrelated `TypeError`** (`dummy.stack.indexOf is not a function`; `.replace` on <= 1.12). Since this runs in the error path, a purely cosmetic step ends up destroying the error it was meant to decorate. The adjacent `err.stack` manipulation a few lines below is already wrapped in `try/catch` for exactly this class of environment — this change applies the same defensiveness to the `dummy.stack` read: ```diff - if (!dummy.stack) { + if (typeof dummy.stack !== 'string') { ``` Repro (before this change): ```js Error.prepareStackTrace = () => ({}); axios.get('http://127.0.0.1:1').catch(e => console.log(e.message)); // "dummy.stack.indexOf is not a function" — real ECONNREFUSED is lost ``` Includes a regression test (`tests/unit/core/Axios.test.js`) that fails without the fix and passes with it. Full unit project passes: 55 files, 976 tests. Real-world impact example: n8n users saw failed OAuth2 token refreshes as this opaque TypeError instead of the actual auth error (n8n-io/n8n#26453). --- ## Summary by cubic Makes `axios` request-error stack decoration fail closed so we never mask the real error. Handles non-string or throwing stack hooks and preserves the original request failure. - **Description** - Summary of changes - Wrap stack decoration in try/catch; ignore failures from custom hooks. - Use `typeof dummyStack === 'string'` before slicing; default to empty stack. - Reasoning - Some environments/APM hooks return objects or throw; previous logic crashed and hid the real error. - Additional context - Only affects the error path; normal string stacks behave the same. - Docs: add a note in `/docs/` about compatibility with custom `Error.prepareStackTrace`. - **Testing** - Added unit tests covering: non-string `prepareStackTrace`, throwing `prepareStackTrace`, and throwing `captureStackTrace`; all preserve the original adapter error. - No further tests needed. - Semantic version impact: Patch (bug fix, no API changes). Written for commit e02bd93def49bfc17520379fe8c7cb08cb5f6ce3. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(interceptors): tolerate a falsy handlers array
description: :surfer: ## Change Summary `syncHandlerEntries()` read `handlers.length` unconditionally, so `axios.interceptors.request.handlers = null` made every request throw a `TypeError` where 1.19.0 carried on. `clear()` already guards for that state, and `utils.forEach` returns early on nullish input, so the manager used to tolerate it. `trimHandlers()` and the `handlersLength` write in the `forEach` finally had the same problem, so the shared tail is now one guarded `compactHandlers()` helper rather than three separate null checks. First commit is the failing test, second is the fix. Fixes #11114 ## Verification - `npx vitest run --project unit` — 987 passed, 56 files - `npx eslint lib/core/InterceptorManager.js` — clean - `handlers` set to `null` and to `undefined` now match v1.19.0 (`forEach` is a no-op, requests still go out) - 4000 randomised use/eject/clear/forEach sequences, including mutation from inside the iteration callback, checked against a reference model: no divergence --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes a crash when `axios.interceptors.*.handlers` is null/undefined by tolerating falsy arrays in both `forEach()` and `eject()`. Restores v1.19 behavior where iteration is a no-op and requests still go out. ## Description - Summary of changes - Added `compactHandlers()` to guard falsy `handlers`, trim, and update `handlersLength`. - Guarded `syncHandlerEntries()` to return early on falsy `handlers`. - Updated `eject()` to safely handle falsy `handlers` and reuse `compactHandlers()`. - Replaced duplicated trim/length writes in `eject()`/`forEach()` with `compactHandlers()`. - Reasoning - v1.20 threw a TypeError when `handlers` was nullish; v1.19 tolerated it. - Aligns with `clear()` and `utils.forEach` behavior for nullish input. - Additional context - Fixes #11114. ## Docs - No docs changes required. - Optional: note that mutating `handlers` is internal and null/undefined is ignored. ## Testing - Added unit tests: - `forEach()` does not throw when `handlers` is null or undefined, and is a no-op (no callbacks called). - `eject()` does not throw when `handlers` is null or undefined. - `eject()` behaves normally after replacing a falsy array. - Existing suite passes. ## Semantic version impact - Patch: bug fix restoring prior behavior without API changes. Written for commit f0161c48be0c86d85cd139eda3348553509b09d6. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(types): make default response marker accessible in declaration emit
description: ## Summary Since 1.19.0, `tsc` fails with TS2527 in any project that compiles with `declaration: true` and forwards a generic response type through `request()` or one of its aliases. #11081 added an internal `unique symbol` (`axiosResponseDefault`) as the default for the `R` generic, but that symbol can't be named from the published declarations. When a dependent forwards an unresolved `R`, the returned `AxiosResponseResult` stays unevaluated, and the inferred type ends up pointing at a symbol the dependent has no way to name, so declaration emit fails. openapi-generator's `typescript-axios` template emits exactly this shape and builds with `declaration: true`, so every generated client breaks against 1.19.0. This moves the marker onto `AxiosStatic` in both `index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`, so the emitted conditional can name it as a member of the axios value. The issue suggested exporting the symbol instead. That works for `index.d.ts`, but not for `index.d.cts`, where `export = axios` rejects any extra top-level export, so a shared `AxiosStatic` member keeps both files consistent and keeps the marker off the public named-export surface. Assignability doesn't change; only declaration emit was affected. ## Linked issue Closes #11116 ## Changes - Expose the default-response marker as a `readonly axiosResponseDefault` member of `AxiosStatic` in `index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`. - Add ESM module typings tests that emit declarations while forwarding a generic `R`, covering both the ESM and CommonJS declarations. The CJS suite pins TypeScript 4.9, which doesn't surface this emit error, so the coverage lives in the 5.x suite. #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes TypeScript declaration emit failures (TS2527) when forwarding generic response types through `request()` by exposing the default-response marker as `axios.axiosResponseDefault` on `AxiosStatic`. Restores `tsc --declaration` builds for ESM and CommonJS consumers; closes #11116. ## Description - Summary of changes: Made the default-response marker accessible via `axios.axiosResponseDefault`; updated `index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`. - Reasoning: The unexported `unique symbol` couldn’t be named from published declarations, causing TS2527 when `R` was forwarded (e.g., `openapi-generator`’s `typescript-axios` clients). - Additional context: Exporting the symbol isn’t compatible with `index.d.cts` (`export = axios`), so a member on `AxiosStatic` keeps ESM/CJS typings aligned without changing runtime behavior. ## Docs Add a short note in `/docs/` (TypeScript typings section) explaining that an internal `axiosResponseDefault` marker exists on `AxiosStatic` to support declaration emit, and it’s for type evaluation only (not a user-facing API). ## Testing Added ESM typings tests that compile with `declaration: true` while forwarding a generic `R`, covering both `import` and `require` paths. The CJS suite remains pinned to TypeScript 4.9 (which didn’t surface the emit error); coverage lives in the 5.x ESM suite. ## Semantic version impact Patch: type-only bug fix with no breaking changes to the public API. Written for commit aa32de9a6c700b070d072d7e325222a009273e12. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(interceptors): tolerate nullish handlers in syncHandlerEntries
description: :surfer: Fixes #11114 ## Problem `syncHandlerEntries()` reads `handlers.length` before checking that `handlers` exists, so assigning a falsy value to the public `handlers` array makes every subsequent request throw: ```js axios.interceptors.request.use(config => config); axios.interceptors.request.handlers = null; await axios.get('https://example.com'); // TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length') ``` `clear()` has always guarded with `if (this.handlers)`, and `utils.forEach` returns early on nullish input, so a falsy `handlers` array was a tolerated state on v1.19.0. This is a regression from #11087 (merged, unreleased). ## Fix Three reads were unguarded, not one: - `syncHandlerEntries` — the `else if (handlers.length !== ...)` branch **and** the trailing `internals.handlersLength = handlers.length`. Both now use a `countHandlers()` helper that treats nullish as an empty stack. - `trimHandlers` — returns early instead of dereferencing. - the `forEach` `finally` block — `internals.handlersLength = this.handlers.length` had the same problem and now goes through the same helper. Fixing only `syncHandlerEntries` leaves the `finally` block throwing on the way out of the first `forEach`, so both paths are covered. ## Tests 8 cases, parametrized over `null` and `undefined`: - `forEach` is a no-op rather than throwing - a **repeated** `forEach` stays safe — this takes the `handlers === handlersRef` branch, which is where the stack trace in the report actually lands, and it isn't reached by a single call - `eject` does not throw - the manager recovers once `handlers` is restored to an array All 8 fail on `v1.x` with the reported `TypeError` and pass with this change. ## Verification `npx vitest run --project unit`: **1001 passed, 1 failed**. The single failure is `tests/unit/adapters/fetch.test.js > should not use inherited Symbol.iterator for request headers`, which fails identically on a clean checkout — unrelated to this change. `npx eslint lib/core/InterceptorManager.js` is clean. ## Not included The report mentions two further items from the same change, deliberately left out to keep this focused on the crash — happy to follow up on either: - `eject(String(id))` silently no-ops now that lookups go through a `Map` rather than an array index. - `tests/unit/core/InterceptorManager.test.js:32` indexes handlers by id, which only holds while nothing below those slots is trimmed. No `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md` entry: per `AGENTS.md` that file tracks user-visible unreleased changes, and this crash never shipped — v1.19.0 behaves correctly. Happy to add one if you'd prefer it recorded. --- ## Summary by cubic Prevents a TypeError when interceptor handlers are set to null or undefined by treating them as empty and restoring them on `use()`. Previously `syncHandlerEntries` and the `forEach` cleanup read `.length` unguarded and could crash; now both paths are safe and behavior matches prior tolerant releases. **Details** - Adds `countHandlers()` and uses it in `syncHandlerEntries` and the `forEach` `finally` block to guard nullish stacks. - Makes `trimHandlers()` return early for nullish handlers. - Updates `use()` to initialize a nullish `handlers` array to `[]` so adding a handler recovers the manager. - Changes are limited to `lib/core/InterceptorManager.js`. **Testing and Docs** - Adds 8 unit tests covering null/undefined: `forEach` is a no-op, repeated `forEach` is safe, `eject` does not throw, and adding a handler after a nullish stack works. - Suggest updating `/docs/` to clarify that while `handlers` is public, consumers should prefer `eject()`/`clear()`; if set to `null`/`undefined`, `axios` treats it as empty and `use()` restores it. - Semantic version impact: Patch. Written for commit a56dd3c4674754f594ac4f138845003ea88283e9. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(xhr): flush final progress during the live loadend dispatch
description:
## Summary

Axios 1.7.0 introduced throttled progress delivery. Timer-deferred XHR progress callbacks therefore receive an event whose DOM dispatch has already ended, so `event.currentTarget` is `null`. Consumers that incrementally read `responseText` through `currentTarget` can miss every deferred chunk, reproducing #6796 most visibly in Firefox and Safari.

This change force-delivers one final `onDownloadProgress` callback from the still-dispatching successful XHR `loadend` event. That gives cumulative readers a live target and the complete response while preserving the established behavior of upload, stream-error, abort-reason, and failed-download flushes. XHR implementations without `onloadend` instead replay their pending progress event through the legacy ready-state fallback.

The forced delivery path is explicit rather than inferred from a flush argument's shape. A final callback can also throw or synchronously cancel the request without leaving settlement pending or causing the XHR handler to dereference a cleared request.

Playwright verification covers Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. A `currentTarget`-based reader that previously received only the initial part of a fast stream now recovers the complete payload.

## Linked issue

Closes #6796

## Changes

- `lib/helpers/throttle.js`: keeps ordinary `flush` argument-agnostic and adds an explicit `flushWith` function for replacement arguments.
- `lib/helpers/progressEventReducer.js`: exposes that explicit forced-delivery function without inspecting stream errors or cancellation reasons.
- `lib/adapters/xhr.js`: force-delivers only the successful final download event, replays pending progress in the eventless ready-state fallback, stops cleanly after synchronous cancellation, and preserves prior failure/upload flush behavior.
- `tests/browser/progress.browser.test.js`: uses real `EventTarget`/`ProgressEvent` semantics and adds eight browser regression tests covering live final delivery, complete streamed reads, the ready-state fallback, cancellation, listener exceptions, status-zero failures, upload failures, and deferred `event.target` behavior.
- `tests/unit/helpers/progressEventReducer.test.js` and `tests/unit/helpers/throttle.test.js`: cover explicit forced delivery, pending-event replay, loaded-shaped errors, throwing getters, and the throttle tuple contract.
- `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md` and `PRE_RELEASE_DOCS.md`: record the download-only guarantee and retained failure semantics.

## Testing

- `npx eslint lib/adapters/xhr.js lib/helpers/progressEventReducer.js lib/helpers/throttle.js`
- `npm run test:vitest:unit` — 58 files, 1,045 tests passed
- `npm run test:vitest:browser:headless -- tests/browser/progress.browser.test.js` — Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit; 42 tests passed

#### Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] Deferred documentation recorded in `PRE_RELEASE_DOCS.md`; no public type change
- [x] No breaking API change

Updates `lint-staged` from 17.1.0 to 17.2.0
Release notes

Sourced from lint-staged's releases.

v17.2.0

Minor Changes

  • #1823 ee156cc - The chunking of tasks based on maximum command line argument length has been re-implemented to be more precise. Now the chunking happens based on the final generated command string, instead of just the list of staged files like previously. This benefits mainly Windows platforms and function commands like:

    /** @type {import('lint-staged').Configuration} */
export default {
  "*.ts": () => "tsc", // Run "tsc" when any TS file is changed (for entire project)
};

    Where the spawned command is literally "tsc" without any extra arguments. Previously, this was still chunked when a lot of files were staged. Now, it probably won't be chunked because the length of the command is just three letters.

    Also, native JavaScript/Node.js function tasks won't be chunked at all, when previously they were run multiple times when chunked:

    /** @type {import('lint-staged').Configuration} */
export default {
  "*.js": {
    title: "Log staged JS files to console",
    task: async (files) => {
      console.log("Staged JS files:", files);
    },
  },
};

v17.1.1

Patch Changes

  • #1820 a626a9f - It's now possible to set --max-arg-length=Infinity to effectively disable chunking of tasks based on the number of staged files. The parsing and validation of the numeric CLI options --max-arg-length and --concurrency has been improved.

Updates `playwright` from 1.61.1 to 1.62.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.62.0

🧱 New component testing model

Component testing moves to a stories and galleries model. A story wraps your component in one specific scenario — hard-coded props, mock data, providers — and a gallery page that you serve renders stories on demand. The new fixtures.mount() fixture navigates to the gallery, mounts a story by id, and returns a Locator scoped to the story's root element:

test('click should expand', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount('components/Expandable/Stateful');
  await component.getByRole('button').click();
  await expect(component.getByTestId('expanded')).toHaveValue('true');
});

Pass a story type as a template argument to type-check its props, and use update(props) / unmount() on the returned locator to re-render or tear down within a test.

🛑 Cancel operations with AbortSignal

Most operations and web-first assertions now accept a signal option that takes an AbortSignal, letting you cancel long-running actions, navigations, waits, and assertions:

const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 1000);

await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click({ signal: controller.signal });

await expect(page.getByText('Done')).toBeVisible({ signal: controller.signal });

Providing a signal does not disable the default timeout; pass timeout: 0 to disable it.

🖼️ WebP screenshots

expect(page).toHaveScreenshot() and expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot() can now store snapshots in the WebP format — just give the snapshot a .webp name:

// Visual comparisons store the golden snapshot as lossless WebP.
await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('homepage.webp');

// Standalone screenshots can trade quality for size with lossy WebP.

await page.screenshot({ path: 'homepage.webp', quality: 50 });

page.screenshot() and [locator.screenshot() (https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-screenshot) also accept webp as a type, where quality 100 (the default) is lossless and lower values use lossy compression.

🧩 Custom test filtering with Reporter.preprocess()

New reporter.preprocess() hook runs after the configuration is resolved and before reporter.onBegin(), letting a reporter mark individual tests as skipped, excluded, fixed, or failing through a TestRun object:

title: fix(types): expose the response default marker type
description:
:surfer:

## Summary

Fixes `TS2527` when a declaration-emitting consumer forwards an unresolved response generic to `AxiosInstance.request`. The conditional return type currently depends on an inaccessible private `unique symbol` type, so TypeScript cannot name the inferred type in the consumer's emitted declaration.

This is the type-only follow-up requested when #11117 was closed: the marker is now a public branded interface whose key remains private. Unlike that PR, this does not declare a nonexistent `AxiosStatic` runtime property, and the regression test runs a real `emitDeclarationOnly` compilation.

## Linked issue

Closes #11116

## Changes

- Replace the private unique-symbol alias with a public, type-only branded interface.
- Mirror the type through the CommonJS `axios` namespace without adding a runtime export.
- Add declaration-emitting regression coverage for both ESM (`index.d.ts`) and CommonJS (`index.d.cts`) package resolution.
- Document the fix in the pre-release changelog.

## Regression evidence

- Before: `npm run test:module:esm -- -t 'emits .* declarations'` exited `1`

- After: `npm run test:module:esm -- -t 'emits .* declarations'` exited `0`

## Verification

- `npm run test:module:esm`
- `npx -y node@20 node_modules/mocha/bin/mocha --timeout 10000 'tests/**/*.module.test.cjs'`
- `npm run test:vitest:unit`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run lint`
- `npx eslint tests/module/esm/tests/ts.module.test.js`

## Scope

- 5 files changed, +50 / -2 lines

#### Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason)
- [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`)
- [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above)

title: fix(helpers): detect data: URL base64 as a trailing media type token
description: ## Summary `estimateDataURLDecodedBytes()` decides whether a `data:` URL body is base64 with a substring test: ```js const isBase64 = /;base64/i.test(meta); ``` Both decoders it guards require that token to be **trailing**. The WHATWG data URL processor base64-decodes only when the media type ends with `;`, optional spaces, then `base64` (ASCII case-insensitive), and `fromDataURI()`'s regex requires `;base64` immediately before the comma. A `base64` token anywhere else — most of all a *media type parameter named* `base64` — leaves the body percent-decoded. PR #11061 established the invariant this guard depends on: the estimate may over-report but must never under-report. The base64 *counting* was fixed there; base64 *detection* is the remaining way the invariant is violated. ## Steps to reproduce ```js import estimateDataURLDecodedBytes, { estimateDataURLBufferAllocation, } from './lib/helpers/estimateDataURLDecodedBytes.js'; import fromDataURI from './lib/helpers/fromDataURI.js'; const body = '一'.repeat(2000); // 6000 bytes of UTF-8 const url = 'data:text/plain;base64=x,' + body; fromDataURI(url, false, {}).length; // 6000 (what Node decodes) (await (await fetch(url)).arrayBuffer()).byteLength; // 6000 (what fetch decodes) estimateDataURLBufferAllocation(url); // 1500 <- guard sees 1/4 of it estimateDataURLDecodedBytes(url); // 1500 await axios.get(url, { maxContentLength: 4000 }); // resolves; 6000 bytes decoded ``` The `;base64` substring matched `;base64=x`, so a body that is percent-decoded text was sized as base64 (3/4 of the *UTF-16* length). Every non-ASCII character widens the gap, because non-base64 characters push the estimator onto its raw-allocation fallback while the real decode is UTF-8: | body character | estimate | actual | under-report | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `A` (1 byte) | 1500 | 2000 | 1.33x | | `é` (2 bytes) | 1500 | 4000 | 2.67x | | `一` (3 bytes) | 1500 | 6000 | **4.00x** | | `😀` (4 bytes) | 3000 | 8000 | 2.67x | The same substring test is wrong in the other direction too: `data:text/plain; base64,…` does not contain `;base64`, so a base64 body that fetch decodes was sized as text and could be rejected while under the limit. Reachability, since this touches a size guard: `maxContentLength` on a `data:` URL is not an amplification boundary — the URL string is already in the caller's memory, and the overshoot is bounded by the length of that string. So this is an inaccurate guard rather than an exploitable bypass, which is why it is here and not in a private advisory. Happy to move it if you would rather. ## Changes - `isBase64MediaType()` implements the trailing-token rule (`;` + optional spaces + `base64`, ASCII case-insensitive, after trimming ASCII whitespace) and replaces the substring test. - Renamed `isBase64Whitespace` to `isASCIIWhitespace`: it is the same set the media type trim uses, and both come from the same spec. ## Verification Every media type the two decoders disagree with the estimator on, before and after. `fetch` and `node` are the byte counts the real decoders produce for the body `QUJDRA==` (4 as base64, 8 as text); `ERR` means the decoder rejects the URL, so nothing is allocated: | media type | fetch | node | estimate (before) | estimate (after) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `text/plain;base64` | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 | | `text/plain;BASE64` | 4 | ERR | 4 | 4 | | `text/plain; base64` | 4 | ERR | **8** | 4 | | `text/plain; base64` | 4 | ERR | **8** | 4 | | `text/plain;base64 ` | 4 | ERR | 4 | 4 | | `text/plain;base64=x` | 8 | 8 | **4** | 8 | | `text/plain;base64=` | 8 | ERR | **4** | 8 | | `text/plain;base64;x=1` | 8 | ERR | **4** | 8 | | `text/plain;x=base64` | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | | `text/plain;name=base64` | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | | `text/plain;=base64` | 8 | ERR | 8 | 8 | | `text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64` | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 | | `;base64` | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 | | `base64` | 8 | ERR | 8 | 8 | Differential sweep over 8000 random `data:` URLs (random media types built from `base64`/`BASE64`/`base64=x`/`x=base64`/`charset=utf-8`/… parameters, random bodies over base64, base64url, percent, whitespace and multi-byte characters), asserting `estimate >= actual` against `fromDataURI()` and against real `fetch()`: | | under-reports vs `fromDataURI()` | under-reports vs `fetch()` | | --- | --- | --- | | before | 138 | 1959 | | after | **0** | **0** | Exact (non-over) estimates also rose from 1099 to 1261, so the guard got tighter, not just safer. - `npm run test:vitest:unit -- tests/unit/estimateDataURLDecodedBytes.test.js`: 15/15 pass. The 3 new assertions all fail against the unpatched `lib/` (verified with the tests staged and `lib/` stashed). - `npm run test:vitest:unit -- tests/unit/adapters/http.test.js -t base64`: passes; the new http adapter case also fails against the unpatched `lib/`. - `npm run test:vitest:unit`: 993/995. The 2 failures are in `tests/unit/adapters/fetch.test.js` (`should not use inherited Symbol.iterator for request headers`, `should reject a chunked response that exceeds maxContentLength during streaming`) and reproduce on clean `v1.x` on this machine — they are unrelated to this change. - `npm run lint`, `npx eslint` on the changed files, `npx prettier --check` on the changed `lib/` file and the changelog: clean. (`tests/unit/adapters/*.test.js` and `tests/unit/estimateDataURLDecodedBytes.test.js` are already prettier-dirty on clean `v1.x`, so I left their existing formatting alone.) - `npm run build`: succeeds. ## Notes - I did not touch `fromDataURI()`'s regex, which rejects `;BASE64` and `; base64` — data URLs the fetch adapter accepts. That is a separate adapter inconsistency and a wider behavioural change; the estimator over-reports for those inputs today, which is the safe direction, so this PR leaves them alone. - No public API change, so `index.d.ts` / `index.d.cts` are untouched. #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) — N/A, internal helper only - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) :surfer: --- ## Summary by cubic **Description** Fixes base64 detection for `data:` URLs in the `maxContentLength` pre-check by requiring a trailing `;` + optional spaces (U+0020 only) + `base64`. Also strips tabs/newlines the URL parser removes so estimates match WHATWG and `fetch`, preventing both under- and over-estimates. - Replaced `/;base64/i` with `isBase64MediaType()` that enforces the trailing-token rule (ASCII case-insensitive, spaces allowed, token must be last). - Removed `\t`, `\n`, `\r` anywhere in the URL before estimating; form feed is not whitespace and breaks the token. - Renamed `isBase64Whitespace` to `isASCIIWhitespace`; used only for body parsing. - Minor: return 0 when the input URL is not a string. **Docs** - Update `/docs/` to note: base64 applies only when the media type ends with `;`, optional U+0020 spaces, then `base64` (ASCII case-insensitive). Tabs/newlines are ignored anywhere; form feed is not ignored and prevents base64. **Testing** - Added unit tests covering: - Non-trailing `base64` and `base64` as a parameter are not base64. - Trailing token with spaces/mixed case is base64. - Tabs/newlines anywhere are ignored; form feed breaks the token and sizes as text. - `fetch` adapter accepts spaced/split tokens at the limit and rejects form-feed cases by decoded text size. - `http` adapter rejects `;base64=x` bodies over the limit. **Semantic version impact** - Patch: internal helper fix; no public API changes. Written for commit dd3e2e301245b85f7fa5210b0ac96ea5a1c53b68. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(core): preserve short reconstructed request stacks
description: ## Summary Preserve reconstructed request caller stacks when stack capture produces only one or two frames. Since Axios 1.15.0, the duplicate-stack guard uses an empty suffix when the reconstructed stack has no second newline. Because every string ends with an empty string, the guard incorrectly treats short caller stacks as duplicates and skips appending them. This restores the pre-1.15 fallback of comparing the complete reconstructed stack in that case. ## Linked issue Closes #11131 ## Changes - Use the complete reconstructed stack as the duplicate-check fallback when it contains fewer than three frames. - Add a deterministic regression test with `Error.stackTraceLimit = 2` and an asynchronous adapter rejection. - Record the fix in `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`. - Verified with `npm run test:vitest:unit` (57 files, 997 tests) and `npm run lint` on Node.js 24.17.0. #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) — N/A, no public API or type changes - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) :surfer: --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes dropped caller traces for short request stacks by restoring the full-stack fallback in the duplicate-stack guard. Ensures one- and two-frame caller stacks are preserved during error decoration since `axios` 1.15.0. Closes #11131. **Description** - Summary of changes - Use the complete reconstructed stack when it has fewer than three frames. - Clarify the duplicate-check logic with clearer naming and comments (no behavior change). - Update pre-release changelog entry for the fix. - Reasoning - The guard compared against an empty suffix when no second newline existed, treating short stacks as duplicates and skipping them. - Restoring the pre-1.15 behavior prevents losing caller context on short stacks. - Additional context - Affects error stack decoration only; no public API changes. **Docs** - Suggest adding a note in `/docs/` under error handling explaining that caller stack traces are now always appended, including when the reconstructed stack is only one or two frames. **Testing** - Added a unit test that sets `Error.stackTraceLimit = 2` and triggers an async adapter rejection to assert the caller function appears exactly once in the final stack. - No additional tests needed; coverage focuses on the regression scenario. **Semantic version impact** - Patch: bug fix with no API changes. Written for commit a49e3ce66a07d0e9f44aebc81e23b5fa28530454. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(AxiosHeaders): store a header named __proto__ instead of writing through Object.prototype
description: ## Summary `AxiosHeaders` could not safely store a header named `__proto__`. Direct assignment invoked the accessor inherited from `Object.prototype`, which either discarded a string value or changed the prototype of the headers instance when the value was an array. The fix maps that single field to an own `__Proto__` slot while keeping header lookup caseless. `normalize` also uses a null-prototype deduplication map. This preserves the header without writing through `Object.prototype` and leaves existing behavior for other header names unchanged. The scope remains intentionally narrow. Request config merging still filters prototype-sensitive keys, the Node HTTP adapter still depends on the fields Node exposes, and XHR raw-header parsing is covered separately. ## Changes - map `__proto__` to a safe `__Proto__` storage slot; - keep `get`, `has`, `delete`, iteration, normalization, and serialization caseless; - cover string and array values, sealed instances, copying, deletion, normalization, and instance isolation; - document the fix in `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`. ## Testing Validated in a Node 22 Linux container: - all 65 tests in `tests/unit/axiosHeaders.test.js` passed; - ESLint passed for `lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js`; - the full production build completed successfully; - the wider unit run passed 995 of 1,003 tests. The eight wider-suite failures are in existing network, proxy, and global-state tests. Running the same suite on the clean `v1.x` base produced the same failures plus one additional timeout, so the PR does not introduce them. ## Checklist - [x] Regression tests added. - [x] No public type or API change. - [x] No breaking change. - [x] Pre-release changelog updated. :surfer: --- ## Summary by cubic Stores a header named "__proto__" safely in `AxiosHeaders` by mapping it to "__Proto__", preventing writes through `Object.prototype` that previously dropped string values or replaced the instance prototype with arrays. Reads remain caseless and behavior for other names is unchanged. - Map "__proto__" to "__Proto__" on set; `get`/`has`/`delete` remain case-insensitive. - Use a null-prototype map in `normalize` to avoid inherited keys. - Do not create an own "__proto__" slot, so `Object.assign` and spread cannot trigger the `Object.prototype` setter; sealed instances rewrite safely; array values keep headers usable. - No changes to `mergeConfig` filtering of `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype`, or to adapters. **Docs** - Update `/docs/` to state that "__proto__" is stored as "__Proto__", remains caseless for reads, and that `mergeConfig` continues to filter prototype-sensitive keys. **Testing** - Added 7 unit tests covering storage/lookup, absence of own "__proto__" on assign/spread, sealed rewrites, array values, deletion, normalize, and instance isolation. Semantic version impact: patch. Written for commit db98fe6be8796d619c7113e5cbcfc19c09c3ec60. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(fromDataURI): accept case-insensitive base64 tokens
description: ## Summary Accept the RFC 2397 `;base64` marker case-insensitively in `fromDataURI()`. Browsers and the fetch adapter already decode `data:text/plain;BASE64,SGVsbG8=`, while the Node HTTP path rejected it with `ERR_INVALID_URL` because its parser required lowercase. A minimal reproduction before this change is: ```js fromDataURI('data:text/plain;BASE64,SGVsbG8=', false) ``` The call now returns the decoded `Hello` buffer, matching the WHATWG data URL processor and the existing case-insensitive size guard. This is complementary to #11130, which fixes base64 detection in the size estimator but explicitly leaves `fromDataURI()` casing unchanged. ## Linked issue N/A — focused bug fix with a regression test. ## Changes - Match the trailing `;base64` token with ASCII-insensitive casing. - Cover lowercase, uppercase, and mixed-case tokens with and without a media type. - Preserve the original media type when creating a Blob. - Record the user-visible fix in `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`. ## Verification - `npm run test:vitest:unit -- tests/unit/fromDataURI.test.js` — 15 passed. - `npx eslint lib/helpers/fromDataURI.js tests/unit/fromDataURI.test.js` — passed. #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) — N/A, no public API/type change - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) :surfer: --- ## Summary by cubic Makes `fromDataURI()` accept case-insensitive `;base64` tokens, aligning Node decoding with browsers and the `fetch` adapter.
