title: fix(interceptors): tolerate a nullish handlers array
description: 🏄 ## Summary `syncHandlerEntries()` reads `manager.handlers.length` before checking that `handlers` exists, so replacing `interceptors.request.handlers` (or the response equivalent) with a falsy value throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length')` on every subsequent request. `clear()` already guards with `if (this.handlers)` and `utils.forEach` returns early on nullish input, so on v1.19.0 the interceptor chain was simply skipped. This is an unreleased regression from #11087. In the same code path, `eject()` also stopped honouring index-like string IDs. The handler registry became a `Map`, whose lookups are strict, so the array-index coercion that used to make `eject(String(id))` work now silently leaves the interceptor installed. ## Linked issue Closes #11114 ## Changes - Guard `syncHandlerEntries()` and `trimHandlers()` against a nullish `handlers` array so iteration, ejection, and compaction skip it instead of throwing. - Coerce index-like string IDs back to numbers in `eject()`, restoring the pre-#11087 behaviour without making `eject(null)`/`eject(undefined)` eject handler `0`. - Assert on array positions rather than interceptor IDs in the existing tombstone test, since IDs stop matching array indices once trailing handlers are trimmed (third point in #11114). - Add unit coverage for nullish handlers, index-like string IDs, unknown IDs, and a request-level test asserting a request still dispatches once `handlers` is nullish. - Record the fix in `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md` and stage the README/API wording in `PRE_RELEASE_DOCS.md`, as `AGENTS.md` asks. #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) ## Notes - This overlaps #11118, which fixes the nullish `handlers` crash on its own. Happy to close this or trim it down if you would rather take that one; this PR additionally covers the `eject()` ID coercion regression and the ID-vs-index test assumption reported in the same issue. - No public API or type changes, so `index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts` are untouched. Per `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` is deliberately left alone for an unreleased fix and the wording is staged in `PRE_RELEASE_DOCS.md` instead. - I was not able to run the suite in my environment, so `npm run test:vitest:unit` verification is left to CI. --- ## Summary by cubic Fix interceptor manager to tolerate null/undefined `handlers` and restore `eject()` support for index-like string IDs. Prevents TypeErrors and keeps requests working when `interceptors.request.handlers` or `interceptors.response.handlers` is set to a falsy value. **Description** - Summary of changes - Guard `syncHandlerEntries()` and `trimHandlers()` to skip nullish `handlers`. - Normalize `eject()` IDs by coercing index-like strings to numbers; unknown IDs are no-ops. - Keep interceptor iteration/ejection/compaction stable when `handlers` is nullish. - Reasoning - Restores v1.19.0 tolerance and fixes the Map lookup regression for string IDs (closes #11114). - Additional context - Preserves public behavior; interceptor IDs remain opaque and not array indices. **Docs** - Update `/docs/` interceptor pages to clarify: - Interceptor IDs are opaque; pass the same ID to `eject()`. - `handlers` is internal; replacing it with null/undefined skips that chain. Registering again requires restoring an array. - Index-like string IDs work for `eject()` for backward compatibility; not a recommended pattern. **Testing** - Added unit tests: - Iteration, ejection, and compaction with nullish `handlers`. - `eject()` with index-like string IDs and with unknown IDs (no-op). - Requests still dispatch when `handlers` is nullish. **Semantic version impact** - Patch: bug fix with no public API changes. Written for commit b805676ea16c4b11beb7963e7f6f1ccc663033db. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix: harden runtime option handling
description:
## Summary

Harden runtime option handling against shared-prototype pollution and make Fetch, HTTP/2, proxy bypass, and data URI behavior consistent across supported runtimes.

## Linked issue

N/A

## Changes

- Filter request behavior inherited only from shared prototypes, including a foreign realm's `Object.prototype` when its mutable `constructor` property has been changed, deleted, or replaced by an accessor.
- Preserve an already-safe merged request config by identity through request interceptors, adapters, and `response.config`.
- Normalize interceptor replacement objects with non-terminal application prototypes into null-prototype snapshots while preserving safe inherited fields. Terminal null-prototype ancestors are excluded as a fail-closed boundary.
- Pass fully resolved `Request` objects to custom Fetch implementations and honor `maxRedirects: 0` with manual redirects.
- Support custom DNS lookup for HTTP/2, reject explicit proxied HTTP/2 requests, and remove failed pooled sessions safely.
- Add IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR matching for `NO_PROXY` and harden malformed data URI parsing.

## Intentional compatibility changes

- Interceptor replacements that require sanitization are normalized snapshots. Their original identity, prototype, `instanceof` branding, accessor placement, and descriptor attributes are not retained.
- Custom Fetch implementations receive the authoritative method, headers, body, signal, duplex, and credentials on the resolved `Request`. Those fields are omitted from the second safe `fetchOptions` argument; custom implementations that inspected the second argument must migrate to the `Request`.
- Fetch `maxRedirects: 0` now prevents redirect following. Node may expose the unfollowed 3xx response, while browsers may expose an opaque redirect with status `0` and inaccessible headers.
- Explicit Axios proxy objects with HTTP/2 now reject with `ERR_NOT_SUPPORT` instead of being silently ineffective.
- Media types containing extra slash separators in data URIs now reject with `ERR_INVALID_URL`.
- Fields inherited from a terminal `Object.create(null)` config template are excluded because such a template cannot be distinguished safely from a mutated foreign `Object.prototype`.
- `NO_PROXY=0.0.0.0/0` bypasses proxying for all IPv4 destinations, and `NO_PROXY=::/0` does the same for IPv6.

## HTTP/2 proxy policy residual

HTTP/2 remains direct when proxy policy exists only in process environment variables or an HTTP/1 agent's `proxyEnv`, because `http2.connect()` cannot apply those proxy mechanisms. Deployments that require proxying as an egress boundary should not treat this change as full HTTP/2 proxy-policy enforcement.

## Validation

- Focused utility, prototype-pollution, and Fetch adapter suites: 164 tests passed.
- Full unit suite: 57 files, 1,035 tests passed.
- Browser-headless suite: 57 files, 591 tests passed.
- Source lint passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated.
- [x] Deferred release documentation notes updated; no public declaration changes.
- [x] Observable compatibility changes are called out explicitly above.

## Semantic version impact

Security/runtime hardening with intentional compatibility changes documented above; this PR does not claim complete backward compatibility.

title: fix(AxiosError): inline the wrapped error stack for cause-unaware tooling
description: 🏄 ## Summary `AxiosError.from()` wraps a native failure (DNS lookup, socket error, timeout, aborted request) in an `AxiosError`. The original error is attached as a non-enumerable `cause`, so anything that walks the standard cause chain - modern Node `util.inspect`, the V8 default formatter, recent Sentry SDKs - already sees the underlying failure. Reporters that read only `error.stack` do not: they get the axios frames that constructed the error, which is why the Sentry events in #6670 point at `AxiosError.js in request.onerror` and say nothing about the actual network problem. This appends the wrapped error's stack to `error.stack` behind a `Caused by:` marker so `stack`-only tooling surfaces the real cause. Nothing about `cause` changes. ## Linked issue Closes #6670 ## Changes - Added `appendCauseStack()` to `lib/core/AxiosError.js` and call it from `AxiosError.from()` immediately after `axiosError.name` is assigned, so the materialized stack header uses the final name. - Every read is defensive: a missing, empty, non-string, or throwing `stack` on either side is a no-op, and the assignment is wrapped so a read-only `stack` or a custom `Error.prepareStackTrace` hook cannot turn error normalization into a throw. This mirrors the guard already used for request-stack decoration in `lib/core/Axios.js`. - Appending is idempotent, so re-wrapping nests the section once instead of growing the string on every pass. - Added seven cases to the existing `core::AxiosError` suite: the appended section, section ordering, `cause` still intact, re-wrapping, a wrapped error with no usable stack, and a `stack` getter that throws. - Recorded the change in `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md` and staged the README/API wording in `PRE_RELEASE_DOCS.md`, as AGENTS.md asks. ## Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) ## Notes - The closing note on #7157 said that one would be replaced by a maintainer-led version landing against the current `from` shape, with a working test in the existing `core::AxiosError` describe block and a short doc note on cause-aware vs cause-unaware tooling. I could not find that follow-up on the tracker, so this is an attempt at exactly that shape. Happy to close it if you would rather write it yourself. - No public API or type changes, so `index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts` are untouched. Per AGENTS.md, `README.md` and the docs site are deliberately left alone for an unreleased change and the wording is staged in `PRE_RELEASE_DOCS.md` instead. - Reading `target.stack` inside `from()` materializes the V8 stack string a little earlier than before. Anything that logged the error already materialized it, but flagging it in case you would rather gate this behind a lazy accessor. - One interaction worth a look: `Axios.prototype.request` appends reconstructed caller frames to `err.stack` afterwards, so those frames land after the `Caused by:` block. I left that alone to keep this diff to a single source file, but I am happy to insert before the marker in a follow-up if you would prefer the caller frames to stay adjacent to the axios stack. - I was not able to run the suite in my environment, so `npm run test:vitest:unit` verification is left to CI. I did check the shipped helper against 12 cases out of band (append, ordering, `cause` intact, re-wrap, missing/empty/non-string/throwing stack, idempotency, and message/code/status/customProps left unaffected). --- ## Summary by cubic Inlines the wrapped error’s stack into `AxiosError.stack` under a "Caused by:" section and keeps axios-reconstructed caller frames before it. Stack-only tools now show the real failure while `error.cause` stays unchanged; closes #6670. **Description** - Append the wrapped stack in `AxiosError.from()` via a defensive, idempotent helper; `error.cause` is unchanged. - Export `CAUSED_BY_SEPARATOR` and update `Axios.prototype.request` to splice caller frames before the cause section, so everything after the marker is the wrapped stack. - Reason: many reporters only read `error.stack`; this makes the underlying DNS/socket/timeout error visible without changing structured cause behavior. **Docs** - Update `/docs/` (README error-handling and `AxiosError` reference) to note the new "Caused by:" section in `error.stack`, that `error.cause` remains the canonical link, and the ordering guarantee (caller frames come before the marker). Avoid presenting the marker as a parsing contract. **Testing** - Added unit tests covering: appended cause section, ordering (caller frames before marker), `cause` intact, idempotent re-wrap, missing/throwing wrapped stacks. - Added a `core` test verifying `Axios.prototype.request` preserves the ordering. **Semantic version impact** - Patch (behavior-only; no public API changes). Written for commit f5cc88553387b43c5925a794093dee8572eab387. Summary will update on new commits.

Updates `lint-staged` from 17.2.0 to 17.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from lint-staged's releases.

v17.3.0

Minor Changes

  • #1825 16b3f74 - It is now possible to run multiple tasks in parallel for a single glob by configuring it with an array of tasks (which run sequentially), and then placing another array inside it (where the tasks will run in parallel). The following demonstrates the order tasks will start in:

    {
  "*.ts": ["first", "second", ["third", "third"], "fourth"]
}

    As a concrete example, lint-staged's own configuration is:

    /** @type {import('./lib/index.js').Configuration} */
export default {
  "*": [
    [
      "oxfmt --check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern",
      "oxlint --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern",
    ],
  ],
  "*.ts": () => "tsc",
};

    which means:

    1. for all staged files, run the two commands in parallel with staged filenames appended, for example:
      • oxfmt --check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern lib/index.js
      • oxlint --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern lib/index.js
    2. additionally, if any *.ts files are staged, run tsc without appending any arguments
    3. The two sets of commands also run in parallel

Patch Changes

  • #1829 15f7e53 - During an in-progress merge, files that are unchanged from the branch being merged are now skipped. Technically, files are only included if there are staged changes against both HEAD and MERGE_HEAD.

title: fix(AxiosError): stop deep-serializing http agents in toJSON
description: ## Summary `AxiosError.prototype.toJSON()` deep-copies the whole config through `utils.toJSONObject()`. If the config carries an `httpAgent`/`httpsAgent`, that walk descends into the agent, its live sockets, and each socket's in-flight request and response. Cycle detection is ancestor-path based, so shared subgraphs are re-serialized once per path and the cost climbs sharply with concurrency. Any error logger that calls `toJSON()` (pino, winston, Sentry) pays it on every failed request, and under load the process runs out of heap. This replaces the two agent values with `'[Agent]'` before serializing. `error.config` still holds the real agent, and the rest of the snapshot is untouched. Anyone reading `json.config.httpAgent` now gets that string instead of a partial dump of Node internals. Measured with the reproduction from the issue at 400 concurrent failed requests through one shared agent, `node --max-old-space-size=512`: | | time in `toJSON()` | snapshot size | | --- | --- | --- | | before | 98,478 ms | 2.2 MB | | after | 3.6 ms | 1.6 KB | ## Linked issue Closes #11145 ## Changes - `AxiosError.toJSON()` records `httpAgent`/`httpsAgent` as `'[Agent]'` rather than walking them - regression test that fails without the change, covering the plain and the `config.redact` path - `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md` entry #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) - N/A, no API surface change - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Prevents `AxiosError.toJSON()` from deep-serializing Node agents. Previously, serializing a config with `httpAgent`/`httpsAgent` walked the agent, its live sockets, and each socket's in-flight request/response, causing CPU spikes and OOM under load. Now agents are recorded as `[Agent]` in the JSON snapshot while `error.config` keeps the real agents. - Replaces both own and prototype-inherited `httpAgent`/`httpsAgent` with `[Agent]` using property descriptors, so neither own nor inherited getters are ever invoked; ignores properties from a polluted `Object.prototype`, survives prototype-chain loops, and skips config keys that getters delete while the snapshot is built. - Clones the config through its prototype so an inherited `toJSON` continues to shape the snapshot. - At 400 concurrent failed requests, time in `toJSON()` drops from ~98,478 ms to ~3.6 ms and snapshot size from ~2.2 MB to ~1.6 KB. Closes #11145. ## Docs Add a note in `/docs/` that agent fields serialize as `[Agent]` while the original agents remain available on `error.config`. ## Testing Added unit tests covering `[Agent]` replacement for own, prototype-inherited, and getter-only agents, pre-redaction replacement, preserving inherited `toJSON`, ignoring `Object.prototype` pollution, keys deleted by getters during snapshotting, and prototype-chain loops. ## Semantic version impact Patch: serialized JSON changes for agent fields only; no API change. Written for commit 62425beaae62e008fc7c577bdeedf0e88db0542f. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(core): stop walking agents when serializing an AxiosError
description: Closes #11145. ## Reproduced The script in the issue exhausts a 512 MB heap on this branch's parent: ``` FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory ``` After the change it finishes in 51 ms with 13.9 MB heap used. ## What is actually going on I measured this rather than assuming, since a single agent is not in itself large — `toJSONObject({ httpAgent })` on an idle agent produces about 900 bytes. The cost only appears while other requests are in flight on the same agent, which is what the repro does by calling `toJSON()` inside the `catch`. Serialized size of `error.config`, by number of concurrent requests sharing one agent: | in-flight | serialized `config` | | --- | --- | | 2 | 43 KB | | 4 | 633 KB | | 6 | 3.1 MB | | 8 | 8.9 MB | | 10 | 19.5 MB | Cycle detection in `toJSONObject` is scoped to the current path — it adds on descent and deletes on ascent, deliberately, so that shared references serialize at each occurrence (the comment there points at #7230). An agent points at its sockets, and each socket points back at the agent and at its peers, so every socket gets re-walked once per distinct path through that graph. The number of paths grows with the number of live sockets, which is why the size explodes with concurrency rather than with the size of any one object. Measured after all requests settle, growth is only linear (about 6 KB per request), which is why this is easy to miss in a quiet test. ## The change `AxiosError.prototype.toJSON()` records `httpAgent` and `httpsAgent` as `[http.Agent]` and `[https.Agent]` instead of walking them. Serialized size is then flat at 684 bytes from 2 to 50 concurrent requests. A few deliberate choices: - **Not changing `toJSONObject`.** Its path-scoped semantics are intentional per the #7230 comment, and switching to a global visited set would silently change how shared references serialize everywhere. A node or depth budget would truncate legitimate configs unpredictably. - **Keyed on config fields, not on object type.** Per AGENTS.md, "do not assume browser- or Node-specific globals exist", so this avoids importing or duck-typing `http.Agent`. It also keeps the browser bundle free of Node-specific detection. - **The config is copied, not mutated,** in line with the "do not mutate config objects in-place" rule. The copy is only made when an agent is actually present. - **Both serialization paths are covered.** `redactConfig` happens to be immune already — its `seen` array is global rather than path-scoped — but routing both branches through the same helper keeps `toJSON()` output consistent whether or not `redact` is used. Only the two agent keys change; every other config key, the original config object, and non-object values such as `httpAgent: false` are untouched. ## Tests Added `agent serialization (issue #11145)` to `tests/unit/core/AxiosError.test.js`, building the cross-referenced agent/socket shape that caused the blow-up: - agents are replaced with their labels while other keys survive - serialized config stays under 500 bytes for a cross-referenced agent - the original config is not mutated - non-object agent values are left alone Removing the source change fails the first two; the other two are invariants that hold either way. `npm run test:vitest:unit` — 58 files, 1066 passed, 0 failed (1062 before). `npx eslint lib/core/AxiosError.js` clean. Changelog entry added to `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md` under Bug Fixes, per AGENTS.md. ## Note on the issue text The issue's own analysis is labelled as AI-assisted and unverified, so I checked it independently. The root cause and the bisect to #5247 both hold up. The one detail I would adjust: the effect is driven by concurrent live sockets on the agent, not by agent size on its own — an idle agent serializes to under a kilobyte. --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Stops walking `httpAgent`/`httpsAgent` during `AxiosError.toJSON()` to prevent super-linear growth and OOM when many requests share an agent. Previously it walked live agent/socket graphs; now it substitutes agents with labels while leaving other fields unchanged. - Substitutes agents via a `WeakMap` shared by `toJSONObject` and `redactConfig`; traversal semantics are otherwise unchanged. - Matches by identity wherever reached (aliases, circular refs). A single instance used for both keys is labeled `[Agent]`; otherwise `[http.Agent]`/`[https.Agent]`. - Skips inherited agent keys, tolerates a throwing own agent accessor, and never mutates the config or promotes inherited values; non-object values pass through. - Applies to both redacted and non-redacted serialization paths. ## Docs Suggest updating `/docs/` to note that `AxiosError.toJSON()` now labels agents (`[http.Agent]`, `[https.Agent]`, or `[Agent]`) instead of walking them. ## Testing Added unit tests covering identity-based substitution, alias/circular reachability, shared-agent `[Agent]`, non-mutation, skipping inherited keys/accessors, throwing own accessors, non-object passthrough, and parity on the redaction path. ## Semantic version impact Patch: output shape changes only for agent fields in error serialization; no request/runtime behavior changes. Written for commit e8c01a063a26017b07e722bcbc5679e7ff7f0c1b. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(core): append a caller stack of fewer than three frames
description: Closes #11131. ## Reproduced The script in the issue prints `caller preserved: false` on `v1.x`. After the change: ``` AxiosError: adapter failure at Timeout._onTimeout (reproduction.mjs:10:31) at listOnTimeout (node:internal/timers:635:17) at Axios.request (lib/core/Axios.js:48:43) at async requestFromNamedCaller (reproduction.mjs:7:3) caller preserved: true ``` ## Cause The report is accurate. The duplicate check trims the top two lines from the reconstructed stack and asks whether the existing stack already ends with the remainder: ```js const stackWithoutTwoTopLines = secondNewlineIndex === -1 ? '' : stack.slice(secondNewlineIndex + 1); if (!String(err.stack).endsWith(stackWithoutTwoTopLines)) { ``` With fewer than three frames there is no second newline, so the remainder is `''` and the condition becomes `err.stack.endsWith('')`, which is always true. The append is skipped and the request call site is lost. ## Change An empty remainder means there is nothing to compare, so it should not count as a match: ```js const stackWithoutTwoTopLines = secondNewlineIndex === -1 ? null : stack.slice(secondNewlineIndex + 1); if (stackWithoutTwoTopLines === null || !String(err.stack).endsWith(stackWithoutTwoTopLines)) { ``` Three or more frames take the same path as before. ## Blast radius I captured full stacks across five scenarios before and after — shallow async rejection, deep async rejection, synchronous rejection, an error with an empty `stack`, and a plain `Error` — and diffed them with axios's own line numbers normalised, since the patch shifts them: ``` CHANGED shallow-async(limit2) identical deep-async(default) identical sync-reject(default) identical no-stack-error identical plain-error ``` Only the case the issue describes changes; the rest are byte-identical. Worth noting the trigger is not only an unusual `Error.stackTraceLimit`. The reconstructed stack is captured where `Axios.request` rejects, so an ordinary top-level `await` can produce a two-frame stack on its own. ## Tests Added to `request error stack decoration` in `tests/unit/core/Axios.test.js`: - a caller stack of fewer than three frames is appended, asserting the caller's name survives - an error whose stack the reconstructed one already matches is not appended to, so the existing duplicate suppression still holds Removing the source change fails the first; the second passes either way, which is the point of keeping it. `npm run test:vitest:unit` — 58 files, 1064 passed, 0 failed, against 1062 on the base. `npx eslint lib/core/Axios.js` clean. Changelog entry added to `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md` per AGENTS.md. --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Restores caller stack appending for reconstructed stacks with fewer than three frames and prevents duplicate appends. Previously the duplicate check used an empty remainder for shallow stacks, always "matched," and skipped the append; repeated decorations could also append the short stack twice. Now the full reconstructed stack is compared for shallow stacks and appended only when needed, so request call sites remain visible without duplication. Effect is limited to shallow stacks; three or more frames are unchanged. No API or config changes. ## Docs Add a short note in `/docs/` under error handling/debugging explaining stack decoration and that one- or two-frame caller stacks are preserved. ## Testing - Added unit tests in `tests/unit/core/Axios.test.js`: appends a caller stack with fewer than three frames and preserves the caller name; does not append when the error's stack already ends with the reconstructed stack; does not append a short caller stack twice. - All existing tests pass. ## Semantic version impact Patch. Bug fix to error stack decoration without public API changes. Written for commit 9f1784548ccee8d2b136702808e8b6c85c968562. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(types): export the default response marker for declaration emit
description: Closes #11116. `AxiosResponseDefault` is the default for `R` on every request method. When a dependent forwards an unresolved generic `R`, the `AxiosResponseResult<…>` conditional stays unevaluated, so the inferred type has to name the marker. As a `unique symbol` it is unnameable from outside the package and declaration emit gives up: ``` repro.ts(3,14): error TS2527: The inferred type of 'makeRequest' references an inaccessible 'unique symbol' type. ``` This replaces the symbol with a nameable brand: ```ts export interface AxiosResponseDefault { readonly __axiosResponseDefault__: true; } ``` An interface can be exported through `declare namespace axios` without instantiating the namespace, so the same fix lands on both entry points. Simply exporting the `unique symbol` does not work for CommonJS: `index.d.cts` ends in `export = axios`, which permits no additional named exports, and moving a `const` into the namespace instantiates it and collides with `declare const axios`. This is a type-only export. It adds no runtime binding, and none is required. ## Verification The repro from the issue, compiled with `declaration: true` and `module: nodenext` on TypeScript 5.9.3, resolving through each entry point in turn: | | index.d.ts (esm) | index.d.cts (cjs) | |---|---|---| | `v1.x` | TS2527 | TS2527 | | this branch | clean | clean | I also compiled a consumer covering the ordinary surface — `get` with the default `R`, `get` with an explicit one, `request`, `create`, interceptors, `isAxiosError`. Clean before and after; only the forwarded-generic case changes. `npm run test:vitest:unit` — 58 files, 1062 passed, 0 failed, unchanged. Assignability is untouched: the marker is only ever compared with `extends`, never constructed. I did not add a regression test, as I could not find any declaration-emit type tests in the repo to extend. A small fixture compiled with `--declaration` in CI would catch this class of problem; happy to add one in whatever shape you prefer. --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Exports a nameable default response marker so TypeScript `--declaration` emit works in dependents. Previously a hidden `unique symbol` in inferred return types caused TS2527 when dependents forwarded an unresolved generic `R`; now a branded `AxiosResponseDefault` interface is available in both ESM and CJS declarations. This is a type-only change with no runtime behavior differences. - Replaces the `unique symbol` marker with an exported `AxiosResponseDefault` interface that types can name. - ESM exports it from `index.d.ts`; CJS declares it inside `declare namespace axios` and references it via a top-level type alias, since `export =` forbids additional named exports. - Preserves `AxiosResponseResult` conditional behavior and assignability. Adds a changelog entry. ## Docs Add a `/docs/` note that `AxiosResponseDefault` is a named type in ESM and CJS declarations; no runtime export. ## Testing No new tests. Verified a consumer with `--declaration` succeeds for forwarded-generic `R`; unit tests unchanged. Consider a CI fixture compiling a minimal dependent against both module systems. ## Semantic version impact Patch — type-only fix with no runtime or public API changes. Written for commit d8b9019c49d4937458a683ce8dee42d6669061ba. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(core): avoid mutating caller's config object in axios(url, config)
description: ## Summary - `Axios#_request()` wrote `url` directly onto the `config` object passed by the caller when using the `axios(url, config)` shorthand (e.g. `axios('example/url', config)`), silently mutating an object the library does not own. - This is easy to hit by accident: `const shared = {...}; axios('/first', shared); axios('/second', shared);` leaves `shared.url` set to `'/second'` afterwards, even though the caller never asked for that field to be added. - Fixed by building a shallow copy (`config = { ...config, url: configOrUrl }`) instead of mutating in place, consistent with the project's existing "do not mutate config objects" convention used elsewhere in `mergeConfig`/`utils.merge`. ## Test plan - [x] Added a regression test in `tests/unit/axios.test.js` asserting the original `config` object is unchanged (no `url` key added) after `axios.request(url, config)`. - [x] `npm run test:vitest:unit` — full unit suite passes (one pre-existing, unrelated failure in `tests/unit/adapters/fetch.test.js` reproduces identically on `v1.x` without this change). - [x] `npx eslint lib/core/Axios.js tests/unit/axios.test.js` — clean. - [x] Added a `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md` entry under Bug Fixes. :surfer: --- ## Summary by cubic Prevents `axios(url, config)` from mutating the caller’s config and from invoking unsafe getters. Previously `_request` wrote `url` onto the provided object; now it builds a fresh null-prototype copy that copies only enumerable own keys (including symbols) and skips `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype`. ## Description - Summary: Copy only enumerable own keys (incl. symbols), skip unsafe names before reading, and avoid non-enumerables; use a null-prototype target to prevent inherited `Object.prototype` setters from intercepting assignments. - Reasoning: Preserve caller ownership, mirror native object spread semantics, and align with `mergeConfig` behavior. - Additional context: Handles the no-config shorthand call and guards proxies that report symbol keys without descriptors. ## Docs - Update `/docs/` (request configuration and `axios(url, config)` shorthand) to state the input config is not mutated, only enumerable own keys are read, and `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` are ignored. ## Testing - Added regression tests: input config remains unchanged; unsafe key getters aren’t invoked; non-enumerable getters aren’t read; shorthand works without a config; proxy phantom symbol doesn’t throw; inherited `Object.prototype` setter isn’t invoked. - Full unit suite passes; one unrelated fetch adapter test still fails on `v1.x`. ## Semantic version impact Patch (no API changes). Written for commit e13093509e94224fe5e05cc9c034415edcefd35f. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(core): keep literal request headers named after a method
description:
## Summary

Request preparation strips `common` and method-named keys from the merged headers so that per-method defaults do not leak as literal headers. Since #11096 that list covers every entry in the new `methodList`, which added `options`, `purge`, `link`, and `unlink`. The removal is unconditional, so a **literal** request header whose name matches one of those methods is now deleted instead of being sent.

`Link` is the case that matters in practice: it is a real request header (RFC 8288), used for example by Linked Data Platform clients sending `Link: <http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#Resource>; rel="type"` on `POST`/`PUT`. Because header names are lowercased while configs are merged, both `link` and `Link` are affected. The capitalization the caller used makes no difference.

Reproduced against a local server that echoes back the received request headers:

```
### BEFORE #11096 (e6824ee~1):
SENT     link (lowercase)
SENT     Link (capitalized)
SENT     unlink
SENT     purge
SENT     options
SENT     x-custom (control)

### main (e6824ee):
DROPPED  link (lowercase)
DROPPED  Link (capitalized)
DROPPED  unlink
DROPPED  purge
DROPPED  options
SENT     x-custom (control)
```

The fix keys off the value shape rather than the name. A `common` or method key is a structural default bucket only when it holds an object; a string, number, or array under the same name is a header value the caller asked to send. Nullish values are still stripped, so `defaults.headers` behaviour is unchanged.

#11096 shipped in [1.20.0](https://github.com/axios/axios/releases/tag/v1.20.0), so this regression is in that release.

## Linked issue

None. Found while reading the `methodList` change in #11096.

## Changes

- `lib/core/Axios.js`: treat a `common` or method key as a header bucket only when it holds an object; strip only those keys, and only merge those into the context headers.
- `tests/unit/axios.test.js`: regression test asserting that `link`/`Link` and `options`, `purge`, `unlink`, `query` literal header values reach the adapter.
- `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`: entry under Bug Fixes, per `AGENTS.md`. Happy to fold it into the existing #11096 entry instead if you would rather not list the follow-up separately.

#### Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason)
- [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`): N/A, no public API change
- [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above)

### Test evidence

The new test fails on `main` and passes with the change:

```
 FAIL  |unit| tests/unit/axios.test.js > Axios > should send a literal header that shares its name with a method
AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal:
+ actual - expected

+ undefined
- '<http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#Resource>; rel="type"'

 ❯ tests/unit/axios.test.js:140:14
```

`npm run test:vitest:unit` after the change:

```
 Test Files  58 passed (58)
      Tests  1063 passed (1063)
```

`npm run lint` reports no problems, and `prettier --check` passes on the changed files.

title: fix(auth): UTF-8 encode basic auth username to match password encoding
description: ## Summary `resolveConfig` build the basic auth header as `btoa(username + ':' + encodeUTF8(password))` — it UTF-8 encodes the password but passes the username to `btoa` raw, so the two halves of the same credential are encoded inconsistently. - A username char in U+0080..U+00FF is emitted as single Latin-1 byte instead of its UTF-8 sequence (`naïve` → `0xEF` where password half correctly gives `0xC3 0xAF`), so a server decoding per RFC 7617 gets broken username. - A username char above U+00FF makes `btoa` throw `ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE` — even though the same char is handled fine in password. RFC 7617 base64-encodes the octet form of `user-id:password`, so both fields need same treatment. This encodes both with `encodeUTF8`. `encodeUTF8('')` is `''`, so empty-credential behavior is unchanged, and the existing lone-surrogate rejection still throws. ## Linked issue N/A ## Changes - Encode the Basic auth username with `encodeUTF8`, matching the password - Add regression tests: a non-ASCII username round-trips, and a beyond-Latin-1 username no longer throws #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated - [ ] Docs/types updated if public API changed (N/A — no public API change) - [x] No breaking changes --- ## Summary by cubic UTF-8 encodes the Basic auth username in `resolveConfig` to match the password and RFC 7617. Previously the username went to `btoa` raw, which mis-encoded U+0080..U+00FF and threw for >U+00FF; now both fields use `encodeUTF8`, fixing non-ASCII usernames without changing empty-credential behavior. - Description - Encodes `username` with `encodeUTF8` and builds `Authorization: Basic ...` from UTF-8 `user:pass` per RFC 7617. - Preserves empty-credential behavior; still wraps invalid encoding as `AxiosError.ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE`. - Docs: optional note in `/docs/` to state both Basic auth fields are UTF-8 encoded. - Semantic version impact: patch. - Testing - Added two regression tests in `tests/unit/helpers/resolveConfig.test.js`: non-ASCII username round-trips; characters beyond Latin-1 no longer throw. Written for commit 0735af41259f8337bf8319557f0cb10dfa8e408e. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(buildURL): reject nullish url instead of coercing it to an empty string
description:
## Summary

#10959 added `url = url || ''` to `buildURL` to stop a `TypeError` when params were passed with an undefined url. That guard also changed what a nullish url means. `axios.get(null, { params })` used to blow up before any request went out; since 1.18.1 it builds `?foo=bar`, which the browser resolves against the current page, so the app silently fires a request at itself.

The empty string is a legitimate relative url and should keep working. `null` and `undefined` are not, and they should not quietly become one. This restores the fail-fast behavior without bringing back the raw `TypeError`: a non-string url with params now throws an `AxiosError` carrying `ERR_INVALID_URL`, the same code `buildFullPath` already uses for unusable urls. Values such as `0`, `false` and a `URL` instance previously reached `url.indexOf` and died with a bare `TypeError`, so they are covered by the same check. A url that comes from `baseURL` alone is unaffected, since `combineURLs` has already turned it into a string by then.

Scope is deliberately limited to the params path, which is the part #10959 changed. `axios.get(null)` without params returns early at `if (!params)` and behaves exactly as it did before 1.18.1.

## Linked issue

Closes #11160

## Changes

- `lib/helpers/buildURL.js`: throw `AxiosError` / `ERR_INVALID_URL` for a non-string url instead of coercing it to `''`.
- `tests/unit/helpers/buildURL.test.js`: cover the rejection and keep the empty-string case explicit.
- `tests/unit/helpers/resolveConfig.test.js`: regression test for the reported path, a null url plus params no longer resolves to the current page.
- `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`: note the fix.

## Testing

- `npx eslint lib/helpers/buildURL.js`
- `npm run test:vitest:unit` — 58 files, 1,064 tests passed

#### Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] No public API type change
- [x] Behavior change is intentional and restores pre-1.18.1 semantics for nullish urls

title: fix: normalize parsed protocols to lowercase
description: ## Summary Normalize parsed URL protocols to lowercase. URL schemes are case-insensitive, but the browser adapter compares the parsed value against a lowercase allowlist. As a result, valid uppercase schemes such as HTTP: and DATA: could be rejected as unsupported. ## Linked issue N/A - strict, self-contained bug fix. ## Changes - Lowercase matched protocols in parseProtocol. - Add regression coverage for uppercase HTTP and DATA schemes. #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (N/A; no public API change) - [x] No breaking changes Validation: npm run test:vitest:unit -- tests/unit/parseProtocol.test.js tests/unit/fromDataURI.test.js; focused ESLint passed. :surfer: AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex was used to identify, implement, and validate this fix. The account owner explicitly requested the contribution and will handle maintainer follow-up. --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Normalizes parsed URL protocols to lowercase so case-insensitive schemes are accepted consistently. title: build!: migrate release bundles to Rolldown
description:
## Summary

Replaces the Axios v2 release bundler with standalone Rolldown while preserving the existing ESM, browser and Node CommonJS, and UMD package surfaces.

This intentionally raises generated browser bundle syntax from ES5 to ES2018. The existing UMD paths, classic-script axios global, AMD support, and jsDelivr/unpkg defaults remain unchanged. Axios v1.x remains the fallback for consumers that require ES5 syntax.

## Linked issue

N/A. The approved implementation record is Plan 002 in docs/plans.

## Changes

- Replace Rollup, Babel, Terser, and their build plugins with exact rolldown 1.2.4.
- Replace Gulp cleanup and release-version orchestration with focused native Node.js scripts, removing Gulp and fs-extra.
- Prepare release metadata in npm's `version` hook after the manifest bump and stage the generated version file with the release commit; scripts-disabled CI runs `prepare:version` explicitly. Refresh contributors before writing release files, with a per-request timeout and warning plus cached contributors on GitHub failures. Stage both release files, roll back failed replacements, retain backups if rollback fails, and preserve the manifest newline.
- Preserve all six JavaScript bundles and two minified source maps with explicit browser and Node platforms.
- Add generated-artifact contracts for file inventory, ES2018 syntax, UMD global and AMD loading, exports, source maps, and platform separation.
- Run artifact validation after building and before packing in the `build-and-run-vitest` jobs of pull-request CI (`run-ci.yml`) and `release-branch.yml`.
- Validate the final build after version preparation before creating a release PR, and validate the tag-triggered publish build before npm staging.
- Align contributor and threat-model guidance with these checks and the parallel test jobs. Document manual knowledge-base refresh, evidence recording, and conditional plan archival steps.
- Reduce the clean root dependency installation from 629 packages to 339 without changing runtime dependencies.

## Validation

Verified on 2026-09-09 with Node 24.18.0:

- A fresh `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `npm run build`, and all 22 generated-artifact checks pass.
- All 21 focused release regressions pass: actual npm patch/minor/major/prerelease lifecycles retain matching metadata, build output, contributors, and release commits/tags; GitHub failures keep cached contributors and allow version preparation. Injected partial writes, backup failures, replacement failures, and rollback failures verify original-file recovery and retained backups.
- With local contributor stubs, both the full npm version lifecycle and the scripts-disabled CI sequence build prerelease bundles that pass all 22 artifact checks. The lifecycle tag contains matching version metadata and refreshed contributors. Deliberately incorrect UMD version metadata is rejected with a nonzero exit.

title: fix(core): append reconstructed caller stack when it has fewer than 3 frames
description:
Fixes #11131.

## What

`Axios.prototype.request`'s `catch` block reconstructs a fresh caller stack via `Error.captureStackTrace(dummy)` and appends it to the original error's `.stack`, skipping the append only when it would duplicate what's already there. The duplicate check compares the original stack's tail against the reconstructed stack's own content *after its first two lines* -- the idea being: if the original stack already ends with those deeper, shared ancestor frames, appending would be pure duplication.

When the reconstructed stack has fewer than 3 lines (a reduced `Error.stackTraceLimit`, or just a shallow call chain -- easy to hit with async adapters), there's no "remainder after the top two lines", so that comparison target became `''`. Every string trivially ends with `''`, so the append was always skipped -- the reconstructed caller context was silently dropped in exactly the case (a shallow, distinct-origin stack) it exists to help most.

## Fix

One-line change: when there's no third line to slice from, compare against the *full* reconstructed stack instead of `''`, matching the semantics already used for the 3+-frame case.

```diff
- secondNewlineIndex === -1 ? '' : stack.slice(secondNewlineIndex + 1);
+ secondNewlineIndex === -1 ? stack : stack.slice(secondNewlineIndex + 1);
```

## Testing

- Added two tests to `tests/unit/core/Axios.test.js` (matching its existing "request error stack decoration" pattern -- a real `axios.request()` call with a custom rejecting `adapter`, not mocked internals) covering `Error.stackTraceLimit` set to 1 and 2. Both assert the reconstructed stack (`Axios.request`, which only appears in the freshly-captured portion -- the adapter error's own stack never contains it) is present, rather than silently dropped.
- Verified as a negative control: both new tests fail on unfixed source with exactly the reported symptom (reconstructed stack missing), and pass with the fix.
- Ran the full unit suite (`npm run test:vitest:unit`): 1064/1064 passing, no regressions.
- `npx eslint lib/core/Axios.js tests/unit/core/Axios.test.js`: clean.

## Notes for review

- Before finding the actual bug location, I initially branched from this repo's `main` branch, which turned out to be a stale/legacy branch with an entirely different (mocha/karma) test layout -- re-based the work onto `v1.x` (the real default/active branch) once I caught the mismatch. Flagging in case it's useful signal that `main` being stale/confusing for new contributors is worth a look, independent of this PR.
- Added a `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md` entry under "Bug Fixes" per `AGENTS.md`'s guidance for unreleased user-visible changes.

title: fix: code quality improvements across lib
description: - Fix double assignment in AxiosHeaders.accessor() that always overwrites internal state instead of preserving existing accessors - Correct JSDoc for isArray in utils.js which incorrectly described it as checking for non-null objects instead of arrays - Fix grammar error in toFormData.js JSDoc (a array -> an array) - Rename misleading callback parameters in adapters.js (fn, value) to (adapter, name) to match what forEach actually passes - Extract duplicated encodeUTF8 function from fetch.js and resolveConfig.js into shared lib/helpers/encodeUTF8.js - Extract duplicated decodeURIComponentSafe function from fetch.js and http.js into shared lib/helpers/decodeURIComponentSafe.js - Remove dead code: lib/helpers/deprecatedMethod.js and lib/env/classes/FormData.js which were never imported anywhere - Added regression tests for the accessor fix, covering repeated accessor() calls preserving existing registrations, subclass registrations isolated from the parent, and sibling subclasses not leaking registrations to each other or the parent. --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Fixes `AxiosHeaders.accessor()` and other code quality issues across `lib`. `AxiosHeaders.accessor()` previously used a double assignment that always reset internal state, discarding any registered accessors. The first fix used `this[$internals] || {}`, but for subclasses `$internals` resolves through the prototype chain to the parent's truthy object, so subclasses kept mutating the parent's shared accessors map. It now uses `utils.hasOwnProp()` so each constructor owns its own internals object and accessor registration can't leak across constructor boundaries. - `utils.js` JSDoc for `isArray` now correctly describes an Array check, not a non-null object check. - `adapters.js` callback params renamed `(fn, value)` to `(adapter, name)` to match what `forEach` actually passes. - Extracted duplicated `encodeUTF8` and `decodeURIComponentSafe` into shared `lib/helpers/` modules; `fetch.js`, `http.js`, and `resolveConfig.js` now import them. - Removed `lib/helpers/deprecatedMethod.js` and `lib/env/classes/FormData.js`, which were never imported anywhere in the codebase. - Fixed JSDoc grammar in `toFormData.js` ("a array" → "an array"). Reasoning: reduces duplication, corrects misleading docs, and fixes a latent bug that could break custom header accessors and leak state between constructors. ## Docs No documentation updates needed; all changes are internal refactors and comment fixes. ## Testing Added regression tests for the accessor fix, covering repeated `accessor()` calls preserving existing registrations, subclass registrations isolated from the parent, and sibling subclasses not leaking registrations to each other or the parent. ## Semantic version impact The removed module files are deep-importable, so consumers importing those paths directly would break; this is treated as an intentional major (breaking) change. No other public API changes. Written for commit aae4d5a84ef5b6c7c368eba4ee70e5d20b080b31. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix: harden request option resolution and no_proxy matching
description: Three related hardening fixes on the v0.x line. ## Form serializer options `toFormData` merged caller options onto a plain object and then read `visitor`, `maxDepth`, `dots`, `indexes`, `metaTokens` and `Blob` directly from it. Inherited values could choose the serializer visitor, the depth limit and the key format, and could also mask an option the caller had set. Options are now materialised on a null-prototype object holding only own, defined properties from the caller. ## Request method, headers and redirect hooks - The default instance method fallback read `this.defaults.method`, so an inherited value could replace the default `GET` on `axios.request({ url })` and `axios({ url })`. Method aliases and explicit methods were never affected. - `dispatchRequest` read `config.headers`, which a request interceptor may replace with an object that has no own `headers`. - The HTTP adapter kept its redirect hooks on a plain object. The `config` hook is only populated when the caller supplies `beforeRedirect`, so an inherited function could reach the redirect path and rewrite the request target. The first two are now read as own properties, and the redirect hook bag has a null prototype. ## no_proxy matching - Trailing-dot normalisation used an anchored `/\.+$/`, which backtracks quadratically on a long run of dots that is not at the end of the string. Hostnames reach this helper from redirect `Location` values, so the cost needs to stay linear. Replaced with a linear scan: 100k dots now normalises in about 1ms. - CIDR entries such as `10.0.0.0/8` were compared as literal hostnames and so never matched, meaning traffic operators had excluded still went through the proxy. IPv4 and IPv6 ranges are now parsed and matched on address bits. - Dotted-quad octets carrying leading zeros are rejected. The URL parser reads `010.0.0.1` as octal `8.0.0.1`, so a decimal read of the same literal in an entry would cover hosts the operator never named. `isLoopbackIPv4` stays deliberately permissive, since a leading zero in a later octet cannot change whether the first octet is `127`. ## Compatibility `NO_PROXY` entries in CIDR form previously matched nothing and now take effect. Traffic that used to traverse the proxy will stop doing so wherever operators wrote ranges. That is the documented intent of the setting, but it is a live routing change and should be called out in the release notes. Two narrower changes: instance defaults that inherit `method` from a custom prototype no longer apply, and an interceptor returning an object that inherits `headers` no longer picks those up. No declaration changes, so `index.d.ts` and the dtslint fixtures are untouched. ## Testing - `grunt eslint mochaTest`: 202 passing, lint clean. - `grunt karma:single`: 335 passing on Firefox. - New regression tests were run against the branch point. 19 across the proxy and prototype-pollution suites fail there, so they guard the behaviour rather than describe it. - Differential runs against the branch point on inputs unrelated to these fixes show no behaviour change: 594 `shouldBypassProxy` cases, 196 `toFormData` cases, and 13 full request-path cases covering redirects, `maxRedirects: 0`, instance defaults, interceptors and params. --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Fixes three related hardening issues on the v0.x line: polluted `Object.prototype` values can no longer influence form serialization, request method selection, request headers, or HTTP redirect hooks; CIDR-form `no_proxy` entries (like `10.0.0.0/8`) now match by address instead of by literal hostname; and trailing-dot normalization no longer backtracks quadratically on attacker-controlled redirect locations. - Form serializer options are now read from a null-prototype object holding only own, defined caller properties, so inherited values cannot pick the visitor, depth limit, key format, or `Blob` implementation. - The default instance method fallback and `dispatchRequest` headers are read as own properties, and the HTTP adapter's redirect hook bag has a null prototype. - CIDR entries are parsed and matched for IPv4 and IPv6, leading-zero octets are rejected since the URL parser reads them as octal, and 100k trailing dots now normalize in about 1ms. - Malformed IPv6 ranges now fail closed instead of parsing as a valid network: a dotted quad cannot precede `::`, and `::` must stand for at least one group of zeros. CIDR `no_proxy` entries previously never matched, so this is a behavior change: hosts inside a listed range will now correctly bypass the proxy. ## Docs Suggest documenting CIDR range support for `no_proxy` entries in the `/docs/` directory. ## Testing Adds tests covering inherited-option protection for form serialization and the request path, redirect hook safety, IPv4/IPv6 CIDR matching edge cases including malformed ranges, a scaling assertion for trailing-dot normalization, and a Blob pollution test that fails without the fix. ## Semantic version impact Patch release: no public API signatures change, and the behavior fixes correct previously broken paths rather than removing supported functionality. Written for commit 4d247cf9dc2ed69ecce2988dc8b30cba7ac234ca. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(helpers): treat explicit port 0 as a real port in shouldBypassProxy
description: ## Summary `shouldBypassProxy` used `value || fallback` to compute ports on both sides of the `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` comparison, which treats an explicit port `0` the same as "no port given" because `0` is falsy in JavaScript. This produces two incorrect outcomes: - A request URL with an explicit `:0` (e.g. `http://example.com:0/`) had its port silently replaced with the protocol's default port (80 for `http`), so it could incorrectly match a `NO_PROXY` entry scoped to that default port. - A `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` entry with an explicit `:0` (e.g. `example.com:0`) had its port requirement dropped entirely, so it matched a request to `example.com` on *any* port instead of only port `0`. Both were verified with small repro scripts against the current source before and after the fix. ## Linked issue None — found via manual code review, no existing issue. ## Changes - `lib/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.js`: compute the request port from `parsed.port !== ''` instead of `Number.parseInt(parsed.port, 10) || ...`, since the WHATWG `URL` parser reports port `0` as the string `"0"` (truthy as a string, falsy once parsed to a number) and an unset/default-matching port as `""`. - `lib/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.js`: change `parseNoProxyEntry`'s "no port in this entry" sentinel from `0` to `null` so an explicit `:0` in a `NO_PROXY` entry is distinguishable from "no port restriction". - `tests/unit/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.test.js`: added two regression tests covering both directions of the bug. - `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md`: added a Bug Fixes entry per `AGENTS.md`. #### Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) — N/A, internal helper, no public API change - [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) :surfer: --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Makes `shouldBypassProxy` treat an explicit port `0` as a real port instead of "unset" on both sides of the `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` comparison. - Summary of changes - Previously a request URL with `:0` silently fell back to the protocol's default port (e.g. 80 for `http`), so it could incorrectly match a `NO_PROXY` entry scoped to that default port. Now the request port is read directly from the URL string. - Previously a `NO_PROXY` entry with an explicit `:0` had its port requirement dropped and matched every port. Now it restricts the bypass to port 0 only. - The "no port in this entry" sentinel changed from `0` to `null` so an explicit `:0` is distinguishable from "no port restriction". - Reasoning - Found via manual code review; no linked issue. ## Docs No documentation update needed — internal helper only, no public API change. ## Testing Added two regression tests covering both directions: a request URL with `:0` no longer matches a `NO_PROXY` entry for the default port, and a `NO_PROXY` entry with `:0` only matches requests to port 0. ## Semantic version impact Patch release. Bug fix only, no breaking changes. Written for commit 67e8126f00d118d2afa9cbb3ce46f36dbbf5a97a. Summary will update on new commits.

title: refactor(helpers): remove Internet Explorer detection from isURLSameOrigin
description: ## Summary `lib/helpers/isURLSameOrigin.js` still sniffs the user agent for Internet Explorer: ```js platform.navigator && /(msie|trident)/i.test(platform.navigator.userAgent) ``` and uses the result to skip the port comparison when deciding whether a URL is same-origin (`isMSIE || origin.port === url.port`). This PR removes the IE detection and the port-check bypass. ## Why this is safe to remove - The IE special-casing dates back to **2014** (7aef479, "Adding xsrf protection"), when IE's URL handling required workarounds. The 2024 rewrite to the URL API (#6714 / 0a8d6e1) removed the DOM-parsing workaround but kept the `isMSIE` port bypass. - **Internet Explorer 11 reached end of support on 2022-06-15**, and Trident-based IE modes cannot run current axios anyway (the codebase targets ES2017+). - The project's own **Browser support table in the README lists Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Opera and Edge ("Latest") — IE is not listed** as a supported browser. - Behavior is unchanged for every supported browser: `isMSIE` is always `false` outside IE, so the port comparison already runs everywhere the library supports. The only environment whose behavior would change is one that is no longer supported. - No test references the IE path (`tests/browser/isURLSameOrigin.browser.test.js` covers the same-origin/cross-origin cases, which behave identically after this change). ## Changes - Remove the `msie|trident` user-agent sniff and the `isMSIE` parameter from `isURLSameOrigin`. - Same-origin check now always compares protocol, host and port. Found while auditing long-lived workarounds in popular open-source projects. --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Removes the Internet Explorer user-agent sniff from `isURLSameOrigin` so the same-origin check always compares protocol, host, and port regardless of browser. - IE is outside the supported browser set (end of support in 2022, not listed in the README browser support table), so behavior is unchanged for every supported browser. - No tests reference the IE path, so existing `isURLSameOrigin` browser tests still cover all behavior. ## Docs No documentation update needed; the README browser support table already omits IE. ## Testing No tests were added; the existing browser tests for `isURLSameOrigin` cover same-origin and cross-origin cases, which behave identically after this change. ## Semantic version impact Patch version change: dead code removal only, no behavior change for supported environments, so no breaking or minor impact. Written for commit bcfcb1d44a3a92b3d6b120648343bd913c75eeeb. Summary will update on new commits.

However I can say this will be a draft so code owners can help edit or review this with time before getting it out of the draft stage and into the consideration stage before being merged. ## Linked issue Not Tied to Issue so N/A ## Changes Very Minimal Type-Safety fixes in the examples, other things include rounding up some errors #### Checklist - [ ] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason) - [ ] Docs/types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) - [ ] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above) to be clear this does touch examples, but I don't think much else changed in this release, however its NOT just packages. --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Hardens the example apps and test suite against security issues flagged by CodeQL and updates several development dependencies so new developers don't copy unsafe patterns. - `examples/server.js` resolves request paths against the example root, preventing path traversal outside the examples directory. - `examples/abort-controller/index.html` renders search results with `textContent` and DOM nodes instead of `innerHTML`, removing the DOM-based XSS vector. - TLS tests use the local CA certificate with `rejectUnauthorized: true` instead of disabling certificate validation. - Express test handlers use `res.json()` instead of `res.send(JSON.stringify(...))`. - Dev dependencies were bumped, including `mocha` from 9.2.2 (EOL) to 11.8.0 in `tests/module/cjs`. - The fetch adapter test now sets an explicit `Content-Type` header on the test server response. ## Docs No documentation update needed; public API and library behavior are unchanged. ## Testing Existing unit tests were updated, not added: TLS tests now verify certificates against the local CA, and Express handlers use `res.json()` responses. Verify that the CJS module tests pass under the new `mocha` 11 version. ## Semantic version impact Patch version change. No public API or runtime behavior of `axios` changed; all edits are confined to examples, tests, and dev-only dependencies. Written for commit 3eb4829ef8134dae99c0deca800f05974296be1d. title: fix(fetch): guard against Object.prototype[Symbol.iterator] pollution in header dispatch
description: ## Summary When `Object.prototype[Symbol.iterator]` is polluted, Node.js/undici's internal header dispatch creates a plain `{}` for merged request headers and iterates it with `for...of`. This causes the polluted iterator to inject or overwrite headers (such as `Authorization`). ## Fix In the fetch adapter, check for an own `Symbol.iterator` property on `Object.prototype` right before creating the `Request`/calling `fetch()`, temporarily remove it, and restore its exact property descriptor in a `finally` block. ## Verification - Fixes the failing test: `should not use inherited Symbol.iterator for request headers` - `npm run test:vitest:unit -- tests/unit/adapters/fetch.test.js`: **69/69 passed** - `npm run lint`: **Clean (0 errors)** - `PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md` updated as per guidelines --- ## Summary by cubic ## Description Fixes a prototype pollution vulnerability in the fetch adapter where a polluted `Object.prototype[Symbol.iterator]` could inject or override request headers such as `Authorization` during Node.js/undici's header dispatch. - Detects an own `Symbol.iterator` on `Object.prototype` and temporarily removes it during native fetch dispatch, clearing the value for non-configurable but writable descriptors. - Builds headers as a `Headers` instance or entries array so the `Request` constructor never reads `Object.prototype[Symbol.iterator]` even when the polluted descriptor cannot be removed. - Restores the exact property descriptor in a `finally` block, so in-flight, never-settling, or rejected requests never observe an altered prototype. - Restores the descriptor before invoking custom `env.fetch` or `Request` implementations; native `fetch` is identified by strict identity with the platform fetch captured at module load, so a replaced `globalThis.fetch` is treated as custom while an explicit native `globalThis.fetch` is guarded. ## Docs No documentation update needed; this is an internal security hardening fix. ## Testing Adds regression tests covering concurrent requests, never-settling fetches, rejections, custom `env.fetch` and `Request`, wrapped and replaced `globalThis.fetch`, bound fetches, non-configurable descriptors, and explicit `globalThis.fetch`. All unit tests pass with lint clean. ## Semantic version impact Patch version change. Written for commit 1af49ead2fbe8f6c7252a805c73269ed60f85bf6. Summary will update on new commits.

title: fix(http): apply https.globalAgent TLS options to proxy tunnels
description:
## Summary

A custom CA installed on `https.globalAgent` stops being trusted as soon as a proxy is configured. Requests to an HTTPS origin through a CONNECT proxy fail with `UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY` / `UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE`, while the same request without the proxy succeeds.

`getTunnelingAgent()` forwards TLS options to the tunneled origin only when a per-request `httpsAgent` is set. Without one, nothing is forwarded, so the origin TLS upgrade after CONNECT runs with default trust instead of the trust store the process configured. Without a proxy that connection would be made by `https.globalAgent`, so its options need to reach the tunnel too.

The options are read per request rather than snapshotted, since the tunneling agent is cached per proxy and outlives any single request.

This covers the origin leg only. The proxy's own TLS connection keeps using just the per-request `httpsAgent` options, as it does today, so an HTTPS proxy is unaffected by what sits on the global agent.

## Linked issue

Closes #11176

## Changes

- Fall back to `https.globalAgent` for the post-CONNECT origin TLS options when the request has no `httpsAgent`.
- Add two CONNECT proxy regression tests with a self-signed HTTPS origin trusted through `https.globalAgent.options.ca`, one of them installing the CA after the tunneling agent for that proxy is already cached.
- Record the fix in the pre-release changelog.

## Testing

- `npm run test:vitest:unit` — 58 files, 1064 tests, all passing.
- `npm run test:vitest:unit -- tests/unit/adapters/http.test.js -t "issue #11176"` — fails on the unfixed adapter with `DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT`, passes with the change.
- `npm run lint` — clean.

#### Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (or N/A with reason)
- [x] Docs / types updated if public API changed (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`) — N/A, no public API change
- [x] No breaking changes (or called out explicitly above)

title: fix(fetch): unmask AxiosError on maxContentLength streaming violation and fix Response types
description:
## Summary

Preserve the current request's `ERR_BAD_RESPONSE` when a fetch response exceeds `maxContentLength` and the runtime wraps the stream failure. Keep `env.Response` constructor overrides compatible with Node-only TypeScript projects by deriving the body type from the environment's `Response` constructor.

- Track response-size errors per adapter invocation, including when a runtime drops the original cause. Foreign `AxiosError` causes continue through network-error handling.
- Cover both ESM and CommonJS declarations without DOM libraries, plus native/custom Response constructors, streamed bodies, existing body inputs, and rejection of incompatible constructors.
- Make the affected DNS and chunked-response tests deterministic, and add prerelease changelog/documentation notes.

## Validation

Validated locally on Node 24.18.0:

- `npm run lint`
- `npm run build` and `npm pack --ignore-scripts`
- Fetch adapter unit suite: 72 passed.
- HTTP adapter unit suite: 246 passed.
- Packed-package ESM module suite: 7 passed, including Node-only ESM/CJS and browser declaration checks with TypeScript 5.9.3.
- Packed-package CJS module suite: 8 passed, including constructor compatibility with TypeScript 4.9.5.

## Compatibility

Patch fix: restores response-limit error classification and preserves Node-only TypeScript compatibility. Callers can keep DOM declarations excluded and declaration checking enabled. Existing size limits, default adapter selection, and genuine network-error handling are preserved.
